cards.definition: A vertical asymptote of a rational function occurs where the function becomes unbounded as the input approaches a finite value from at least one side. After common factors are cancelled, remaining real denominator zeros give the usual candidates.
major_error_concepts: Calling every original denominator zero a vertical asymptote even after complete cancellation.
cards.prompt: What is Vertical Asymptote? State its defining idea and essential conditions.
required_concepts: Unbounded approach near a finite input.
Check cancellation before identifying denominator-zero asymptotes.

accepted_variants: A limiting horizontal line at large input magnitude.
cards.definition: A horizontal asymptote is y=L when f(x) approaches L as x tends to positive or negative infinity. For rational functions, degree comparison gives zero when numerator degree is lower and the leading-coefficient ratio when degrees match.
major_error_concepts: Claiming a graph can never cross a horizontal asymptote.
cards.prompt: What is Horizontal Asymptote? State its defining idea and essential conditions.
required_concepts: Finite limiting height at an infinite tail.
Degree comparison for rational functions.

cards.definition: A slant asymptote is a nonhorizontal line whose vertical difference from the graph tends to zero at infinity. For a rational function with numerator degree one higher than denominator degree, polynomial division gives the line.
major_error_concepts: Using the quotient line as the exact function while omitting a nonzero remainder.
cards.prompt: What is Slant Asymptote? State its defining idea and essential conditions.
required_concepts: Difference from a line tends to zero.
One-degree gap gives the usual rational-function case.

accepted_variants: A removable discontinuity caused by a cancelled denominator factor.
cards.definition: A removable hole is an excluded input at which a simplified function has a finite limiting value. Cancelling a common factor can reveal the hole's height but does not make the original function defined there.
major_error_concepts: Filling the hole automatically after cancellation without redefining the function.
cards.prompt: What is Removable Hole? State its defining idea and essential conditions.
required_concepts: Original domain exclusion with finite simplified approach.
Distinguish the original function from its extension.

cards.definition: A rational inequality is solved by a sign chart using numerator zeros and excluded denominator zeros. Multiplying by an expression of unknown sign requires case distinctions rather than preserving the inequality blindly.
major_error_concepts: Multiplying through by an unknown-sign denominator without reversing or splitting cases.
cards.prompt: What is Rational Inequality? State its defining idea and essential conditions.
required_concepts: Partition by zeros and undefined points.
Respect sign changes and denominator exclusions.

accepted_variants: A monomial-type function with a general exponent.
cards.definition: A power function has form f(x)=a x^p for fixed constants a and p on a specified domain. Its parity, real domain, and shape depend on the exponent, especially for negative or noninteger powers.
major_error_concepts: Confusing a^x with a power function of x under this definition.
cards.prompt: What is Power Function? State its defining idea and essential conditions.
required_concepts: Variable base with fixed exponent.
Domain depends on the exponent.

accepted_variants: A constant-ratio function over equal input increments.
cards.definition: An exponential function has form f(x)=b^x with b positive and b not equal to one. It has positive outputs, is increasing for b>1, and decreasing for 0<b<1.
major_error_concepts: Allowing an arbitrary negative base as a real-valued exponential on all real inputs.
cards.prompt: What is Exponential Function? State its defining idea and essential conditions.
required_concepts: Fixed positive base and variable exponent.
Growth versus decay by base range.

cards.definition: An exponential model y=Ae^(kt) has constant proportional change over equal time intervals. Positive k gives growth and negative k decay; this is a modeling assumption rather than a universal property of real populations or quantities.
major_error_concepts: Confusing equal percentage change with equal absolute change.
cards.prompt: What is Exponential Growth and Decay? State its defining idea and essential conditions.
required_concepts: Constant proportional growth or decay.
Sign of k determines direction for positive A.

cards.definition: The compound-interest formula A=P(1+r/n)^(nt) describes a fixed nominal annual rate r compounded n times yearly with no additional cash flows. Continuous compounding uses A=Pe^(rt); the formula is a mathematical model, not a promised real-world return.
major_error_concepts: Treating a quoted model rate as a guaranteed investment outcome.
cards.prompt: What is Compound-Growth Formula? State its defining idea and essential conditions.
required_concepts: Identify principal, rate, compounding frequency, and time.
Assume the stated rate and no extra deposits or withdrawals.

cards.definition: The logarithm log_b(x) is the exponent y satisfying b^y=x, for b positive, b not equal to one, and x positive. It is the inverse of an exponential function on its range.
major_error_concepts: Allowing zero or negative arguments in an ordinary real logarithm.
cards.prompt: What is Logarithm? State its defining idea and essential conditions.
required_concepts: Logarithm asks for the exponent.
Positive argument and valid base.

accepted_variants: Logarithmic product, quotient, and power identities.
cards.definition: For positive u and v and a valid base, log_b(uv)=log_b u+log_b v and log_b(u/v)=log_b u-log_b v. The power rule log_b(u^r)=r log_b u assumes a domain where the expressions are valid.
major_error_concepts: Using log(u+v)=log u+log v.
cards.prompt: What is Logarithm Properties? State its defining idea and essential conditions.
required_concepts: Products become sums and quotients differences.
Maintain positive real arguments.

accepted_variants: Conversion of a logarithm to another base.
cards.definition: The change-of-base formula is log_b x=log_a x/log_a b for positive valid bases a and b and positive x. The denominator is nonzero because b is not one.
major_error_concepts: Reversing numerator and denominator.
cards.prompt: What is Change of Base? State its defining idea and essential conditions.
required_concepts: Log of the argument divided by log of the old base.

accepted_variants: An equation involving logarithms with explicit domain checks.
cards.definition: A logarithmic equation can be converted using inverse exponential relations or valid log identities, while retaining positive-argument restrictions. Candidate solutions outside the original logarithm domain are rejected.
major_error_concepts: Accepting a root that makes an original log argument negative after combining logs.
cards.prompt: What is Logarithmic Equation? State its defining idea and essential conditions.
required_concepts: Use inverse relations while preserving argument positivity.

cards.definition: Exponential and logarithmic functions with the same base undo one another: log_b(b^x)=x and b^(log_b x)=x for x positive in the second identity. Their graphs are reflections across y=x.
major_error_concepts: Applying b^(log_b x)=x to nonpositive real x.
cards.prompt: What is Exponential–Logarithm Inverses? State its defining idea and essential conditions.
required_concepts: Two inverse identities with domain restriction.
Graph reflection across y=x.

accepted_variants: Natural angular measure from circular arc length.
cards.definition: A radian is the angle subtending an arc equal in length to the circle's radius. The relation is theta=s/r, and one full revolution is 2 pi radians or 360 degrees.
major_error_concepts: Equating pi radians with 360 degrees.
cards.prompt: What is Radian Measure? State its defining idea and essential conditions.
required_concepts: Arc length divided by radius.
Full turn equals 2 pi radians.

accepted_variants: The coordinate circle defining trigonometric functions.
cards.definition: The unit circle has radius one and center at the origin. The point reached by angle theta in standard position is (cos theta,sin theta), linking trigonometric values to coordinates.
major_error_concepts: Swapping the sine and cosine coordinates.
cards.prompt: What is Unit Circle? State its defining idea and essential conditions.
required_concepts: Radius one.
Coordinates cosine then sine.

cards.definition: Sine of an angle is the y-coordinate of its unit-circle point. For an acute right-triangle angle it is opposite side divided by hypotenuse, and its values lie between -1 and 1.
major_error_concepts: Using adjacent over hypotenuse as sine.
cards.prompt: What is Sine? State its defining idea and essential conditions.
required_concepts: Unit-circle y-coordinate.
Right-triangle opposite over hypotenuse.

cards.definition: Cosine of an angle is the x-coordinate of its unit-circle point. For an acute right-triangle angle it is adjacent side divided by hypotenuse, and its values lie between -1 and 1.
major_error_concepts: Using opposite over hypotenuse as cosine.
cards.prompt: What is Cosine? State its defining idea and essential conditions.
required_concepts: Unit-circle x-coordinate.
Right-triangle adjacent over hypotenuse.

accepted_variants: The ratio of vertical to horizontal unit-circle coordinates.
cards.definition: Tangent is tan theta=sin theta/cos theta where cosine is nonzero. For acute right-triangle angles it is opposite over adjacent, and its period is pi radians.
major_error_concepts: Defining tangent at pi/2 by ordinary real division.
cards.prompt: What is Tangent? State its defining idea and essential conditions.
required_concepts: Sine divided by nonzero cosine.
Undefined where cosine vanishes.

cards.definition: Secant, cosecant, and cotangent are reciprocal trigonometric functions: sec=1/cos, csc=1/sin, and cot=cos/sin where denominators are nonzero. Reciprocals differ from inverse-angle functions.
major_error_concepts: Equating cosecant with arcsine.
cards.prompt: What is Reciprocal Trigonometric Functions? State its defining idea and essential conditions.
required_concepts: Correct reciprocal definitions and nonzero denominators.
Not inverse functions.

cards.definition: The identity sin squared theta+cos squared theta=1 follows from the unit circle. Dividing on valid domains gives 1+tan squared theta=sec squared theta and 1+cot squared theta=csc squared theta.
major_error_concepts: Using sin theta+cos theta=1 as a universal identity.
cards.prompt: What is Pythagorean Identities? State its defining idea and essential conditions.
required_concepts: Basic sine-cosine identity.
Derived identities preserve denominator restrictions.

cards.definition: The special angles pi/6, pi/4, and pi/3 have exact sine-cosine pairs (1/2,sqrt(3)/2), (sqrt(2)/2,sqrt(2)/2), and (sqrt(3)/2,1/2). These follow from 30-60-90 and 45-45-90 triangle ratios.
major_error_concepts: Interchanging the pi/6 and pi/3 sine values.
cards.prompt: What is Special-Angle Values? State its defining idea and essential conditions.
required_concepts: Correct exact values and angle correspondence.

cards.definition: A reference angle is the acute angle between an angle's terminal side and the x-axis. Trigonometric magnitudes follow the reference angle, while signs follow the quadrant; quadrantal angles are handled directly.
major_error_concepts: Assigning all trigonometric functions the reference angle's positive sign in every quadrant.
cards.prompt: What is Reference Angle? State its defining idea and essential conditions.
required_concepts: Acute x-axis reference angle.
Separate magnitude from quadrant sign.

accepted_variants: The parameterized sine or cosine graph.
cards.definition: A sinusoid y=A sin(B(x-h))+D has amplitude |A|, period 2 pi/|B| for B nonzero, horizontal shift h, and midline y=D. Cosine has the same parameter interpretation.
major_error_concepts: Using 2 pi times |B| as the period.
cards.prompt: What is Sinusoidal Graph? State its defining idea and essential conditions.
required_concepts: Amplitude absolute A and inverse-|B| period.
Midline and shift identified correctly.

cards.definition: Phase shift is the horizontal displacement of a periodic graph relative to its chosen reference form. For sin(Bx-C), factoring the argument shows shift C/B when B is nonzero.
major_error_concepts: Reading C alone as the shift in sin(Bx-C) for arbitrary B.
cards.prompt: What is Phase Shift? State its defining idea and essential conditions.
required_concepts: Factor the input coefficient before reading horizontal shift.

cards.definition: Inverse trigonometric functions return principal angles after restricting the original function's domain. Standard ranges are [-pi/2,pi/2] for arcsine, [0,pi] for arccosine, and (-pi/2,pi/2) for arctangent.
major_error_concepts: Interpreting sin^-1 x as the reciprocal of sine in inverse-function notation.
cards.prompt: What is Inverse Trigonometric Functions? State its defining idea and essential conditions.
required_concepts: Principal-angle branch from an injective restriction.
Standard ranges correctly distinguished.

cards.definition: Angle-sum formulas express sine and cosine of combined angles: sin(a+b)=sin a cos b+cos a sin b and cos(a+b)=cos a cos b-sin a sin b. Difference identities follow by replacing b with -b.
major_error_concepts: Assuming sin(a+b)=sin a+sin b.
cards.prompt: What is Angle-Sum Identities? State its defining idea and essential conditions.
required_concepts: Correct sum formulas and cosine minus sign.

accepted_variants: Trigonometric identities for twice an angle.
cards.definition: Double-angle identities include sin(2x)=2 sin x cos x and cos(2x)=cos squared x-sin squared x=2 cos squared x-1=1-2 sin squared x. They are special cases of angle addition.
major_error_concepts: Equating sin(2x) with 2 sin x for every x.
cards.prompt: What is Double-Angle Identities? State its defining idea and essential conditions.
required_concepts: Correct sine and cosine double-angle identities.

accepted_variants: Half-angle magnitude identities with sign selection.
cards.definition: Half-angle identities give sin squared(x/2)=(1-cos x)/2 and cos squared(x/2)=(1+cos x)/2. Taking square roots requires choosing signs from the quadrant of the half-angle.
major_error_concepts: Always choosing the positive root for a half-angle sine or cosine.
cards.prompt: What is Half-Angle Identities? State its defining idea and essential conditions.
required_concepts: Correct squared half-angle relations.
Quadrant determines square-root signs.

accepted_variants: Solving an angle condition with branch and period bookkeeping.
cards.definition: A trigonometric equation seeks angles satisfying the original relation on the stated domain. Inverse functions give principal candidates, while symmetry and periodicity generate other solutions; transformations can introduce extraneous values or lose branches.
major_error_concepts: Reporting only arcsin(c) as every solution of sin x=c.
cards.prompt: What is Trigonometric Equation? State its defining idea and essential conditions.
required_concepts: Principal values are not always the full solution set.
Account for periodicity and domain.

cards.definition: The law of sines states a/sin A=b/sin B=c/sin C for opposite sides and angles of a triangle. In side-side-angle data, more than one triangle or no triangle may fit, so the ambiguous case requires care.
major_error_concepts: Pairing a side with an adjacent angle or assuming SSA always gives one triangle.
cards.prompt: What is Law of Sines? State its defining idea and essential conditions.
required_concepts: Pair each side with its opposite angle.
SSA data may be ambiguous.

accepted_variants: Cosine rule for a general triangle.
cards.definition: The law of cosines states c squared=a squared+b squared-2ab cos C, where C is the included angle opposite c. It reduces to the Pythagorean theorem for a right included angle.
major_error_concepts: Using an angle not between a and b in the displayed formula.
cards.prompt: What is Law of Cosines? State its defining idea and essential conditions.
required_concepts: Included-angle relation with minus 2ab cos C.

cards.definition: The area of a triangle with two sides a and b and their included angle C is one-half ab sin C. The angle must be the one between the selected sides.
major_error_concepts: Using cosine instead of sine in the included-angle area formula.
cards.prompt: What is Triangle Area from Two Sides and an Angle? State its defining idea and essential conditions.
required_concepts: Half the product of two sides times sine of their included angle.
cards.term: Triangle Area from Two Sides and an Angle

cards.definition: A plane vector has magnitude and direction and can be represented by components (v_x,v_y). Vectors add componentwise, scalar multiplication rescales them, and magnitude is sqrt(v_x squared+v_y squared).
major_error_concepts: Adding magnitudes alone to determine the magnitude of a general vector sum.
cards.prompt: What is Plane Vector? State its defining idea and essential conditions.
required_concepts: Component representation with magnitude and direction.
Componentwise addition and scalar multiplication.

cards.definition: The dot product u dot v equals u_x v_x+u_y v_y and also |u||v|cos theta. It is a scalar; nonzero vectors are perpendicular exactly when their dot product is zero.
major_error_concepts: Treating the dot product as another vector.
cards.prompt: What is Dot Product? State its defining idea and essential conditions.
required_concepts: Component sum and cosine-angle formula.
Scalar result and orthogonality condition.

cards.definition: Parametric equations describe coordinates as functions of a parameter, such as x=f(t), y=g(t). They can encode orientation and repeated traversal that may be lost when the parameter is eliminated.
major_error_concepts: Assuming eliminating the parameter preserves direction and traversal count.
cards.prompt: What is Parametric Equations? State its defining idea and essential conditions.
required_concepts: Coordinates depend on a common parameter.
Parameterization carries traversal information.

cards.definition: Polar coordinates describe a point using radius r and angle theta, with x=r cos theta and y=r sin theta. Representations are not unique because angles repeat and negative radii reverse direction.
major_error_concepts: Assuming one point has exactly one polar coordinate pair.
cards.prompt: What is Polar Coordinates? State its defining idea and essential conditions.
required_concepts: Coordinate conversion formulas.
Polar representation is nonunique.

accepted_variants: Trigonometric or polar form of a complex number.
cards.definition: A nonzero complex number can be written z=r(cos theta+i sin theta), where r=|z| and theta is an argument defined modulo 2 pi. Multiplication multiplies moduli and adds arguments.
major_error_concepts: Adding moduli when multiplying complex numbers.
cards.prompt: What is Complex Polar Form? State its defining idea and essential conditions.
required_concepts: Modulus-angle representation.
Arguments are not unique modulo full turns.

cards.definition: De Moivre's formula gives [cos theta+i sin theta]^n=cos(n theta)+i sin(n theta) for integer n. Combined with modulus powers and all angle branches, it supports powers and roots of complex numbers.
major_error_concepts: Reporting only one root for every nonzero complex nth-root problem.
cards.prompt: What is De Moivre's Formula? State its defining idea and essential conditions.
required_concepts: Integer power multiplies the angle.
Root finding must retain distinct branches.

accepted_variants: Quadratic plane curves of conic type.
cards.definition: Conic sections are curves obtained by intersecting a plane with a double cone; nondegenerate types are ellipses, parabolas, and hyperbolas, with circles as special ellipses. Coordinate equations classify them through quadratic forms and parameters.
major_error_concepts: Claiming every conic must be a closed curve.
cards.prompt: What is Conic Section? State its defining idea and essential conditions.
required_concepts: Plane-cone intersections and the nondegenerate families.

cards.definition: A circle is the set of points a fixed distance r from a center (h,k). Its equation is (x-h) squared+(y-k) squared=r squared with r positive for a nondegenerate circle.
major_error_concepts: Reading r squared itself as the radius.
cards.prompt: What is Circle? State its defining idea and essential conditions.
required_concepts: Fixed distance from a center.
Correct center-radius equation.

accepted_variants: The focus-directrix conic of eccentricity one.
cards.definition: A parabola is the locus of points equally distant from a focus and a directrix. A vertical-axis form is (x-h) squared=4p(y-k), with vertex (h,k) and signed focal displacement p nonzero.
major_error_concepts: Assuming every parabola opens upward.
cards.prompt: What is Parabola? State its defining idea and essential conditions.
required_concepts: Equal distances to focus and directrix.
Vertex and signed p determine opening direction.

cards.definition: An ellipse is the locus whose sum of distances to two fixed foci is constant. A horizontal-major-axis form has (x-h) squared/a squared+(y-k) squared/b squared=1 with a>b>0 and focal relation c squared=a squared-b squared.
major_error_concepts: Using c squared=a squared+b squared for an ellipse.
cards.prompt: What is Ellipse? State its defining idea and essential conditions.
required_concepts: Constant sum of focal distances.
Ellipse focal relation uses subtraction.

cards.definition: A hyperbola is the locus whose absolute difference of distances to two foci is a fixed positive constant. In (x-h) squared/a squared-(y-k) squared/b squared=1, its focal relation is c squared=a squared+b squared and it has two branches.
major_error_concepts: Using the ellipse's sum-of-distances definition for a hyperbola.
cards.prompt: What is Hyperbola? State its defining idea and essential conditions.
required_concepts: Constant absolute focal-distance difference.
Two branches and plus-sign focal relation.

cards.definition: A sequence is a function whose domain is an ordered set of integer indices, commonly the positive integers. An explicit formula gives a term directly, while a recursive definition gives it from earlier terms and starting values.
major_error_concepts: Giving a recurrence without the starting data needed to determine its terms.
cards.prompt: What is Sequence? State its defining idea and essential conditions.
required_concepts: Indexed ordered terms.
Explicit versus recursive definitions.

cards.definition: An arithmetic sequence has constant difference d between consecutive terms. With first term a1, its nth term is a_n=a1+(n-1)d.
major_error_concepts: Using a_n=a1+nd when indexing the first term as n=1.
cards.prompt: What is Arithmetic Sequence? State its defining idea and essential conditions.
required_concepts: Constant additive difference.
Correct nth-term indexing.

cards.definition: A geometric sequence has constant ratio r between consecutive terms where that ratio description is defined. Its standard form is a_n=a1 r^(n-1), with behavior depending on the magnitude and sign of r.
major_error_concepts: Confusing a constant ratio with a constant difference.
cards.prompt: What is Geometric Sequence? State its defining idea and essential conditions.
required_concepts: Constant multiplicative ratio.
Correct nth-term formula.

cards.definition: Sigma notation sums an indexed expression over a specified finite or infinite index range. The index is a placeholder; limits determine which terms appear.
major_error_concepts: Ignoring the lower limit when counting or evaluating terms.
cards.prompt: What is Summation Notation? State its defining idea and essential conditions.
required_concepts: Indexed summation with explicit bounds.

accepted_variants: Closed forms for sums of finite progressions.
cards.definition: A finite arithmetic series has sum n(a1+a_n)/2. A finite geometric series with ratio r not equal to one has sum a1(1-r^n)/(1-r); for r=1 the sum is n a1.
major_error_concepts: Using the infinite geometric formula for a finite number of terms.
cards.prompt: What is Finite Progression Sums? State its defining idea and essential conditions.
required_concepts: Correct arithmetic and geometric finite-sum forms.
Handle ratio one separately.

cards.definition: An infinite geometric series with first term a and ratio r converges to a/(1-r) when |r|<1. Outside that range it diverges unless the series is the trivial all-zero case.
major_error_concepts: Using the formula as a convergent sum for r=2.
cards.prompt: What is Infinite Geometric Series? State its defining idea and essential conditions.
required_concepts: Absolute ratio less than one.
Sum a/(1-r).

cards.definition: For a nonnegative integer n, the binomial theorem expands (a+b)^n as the sum from k=0 to n of binomial(n,k) a^(n-k)b^k. The coefficients count choices and follow Pascal's triangle.
major_error_concepts: Omitting mixed terms and using only a^n+b^n.
cards.prompt: What is Binomial Theorem? State its defining idea and essential conditions.
required_concepts: Correct coefficients and complementary exponents.
Finite formula assumes nonnegative integer n.

accepted_variants: A domino-style proof principle for indexed statements.
cards.definition: Mathematical induction proves a statement for all integers from a starting index by proving a base case and showing that truth at a general index implies truth at the next. Both parts are necessary.
major_error_concepts: Checking several numerical cases and claiming an induction proof.
cards.prompt: What is Induction Principle? State its defining idea and essential conditions.
required_concepts: Base case and inductive implication.
The inductive assumption concerns an arbitrary valid index.

catalog.description: Strengthen algebraic fluency with equations, inequalities, functions, polynomials, rational expressions, exponentials, logarithms, and trigonometry.
catalog.subject: Mathematics
catalog.title: College Algebra and Precalculus

cards.definition: **Definition.** The useful application payload completed per declared interval after protocol overhead retransmission duplication and discarded work.
major_error_concepts: Calling TCP payload bytes application goodput when application framing rejects some data.
cards.prompt: Define Application goodput. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
required_concepts: The useful application payload completed per declared interval after protocol overhead retransmission duplication and discarded work.

cards.definition: **Definition.** The bits required in flight to occupy a specified path at a target rate and round-trip time.
major_error_concepts: Multiplying bandwidth by one-way delay while labeling the result an RTT flight requirement.
cards.prompt: Define Bandwidth-delay product. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
required_concepts: The bits required in flight to occupy a specified path at a target rate and round-trip time.

cards.definition: **Definition.** The minimum effective service capacity along a specified path for a specified traffic class and interval.
major_error_concepts: Averaging link rates or choosing the longest physical link.
cards.prompt: Define Bottleneck service rate. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
required_concepts: The minimum effective service capacity along a specified path for a specified traffic class and interval.

cards.definition: **Definition.** The specified fields and local state selecting the receiving protocol instance endpoint or application.
major_error_concepts: Choosing a process from destination port alone without host or binding context.
cards.prompt: Define Demultiplexing key. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
required_concepts: The specified fields and local state selecting the receiving protocol instance endpoint or application.

cards.definition: **Definition.** The ordered addition and interpretation of protocol metadata around a higher-layer unit at send and receive boundaries.
major_error_concepts: Saying headers are simply stripped by every router or that payload meaning is inspected at each hop.
cards.prompt: Define Encapsulation and decapsulation. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
required_concepts: The ordered addition and interpretation of protocol metadata around a higher-layer unit at send and receive boundaries.

cards.definition: **Definition.** The specified sender receiver client server peer intermediary or router responsibility at one protocol layer and instant.
major_error_concepts: Calling one host permanently client at every layer and direction.
cards.prompt: Define Endpoint role. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
required_concepts: The specified sender receiver client server peer intermediary or router responsibility at one protocol layer and instant.

cards.definition: **Definition.** The interface through which one protocol consumes a lower service while preserving separate peer semantics and implementation state.
major_error_concepts: Drawing stacked boxes and transferring reliability or security across every boundary.
cards.prompt: Define Layer service boundary. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
required_concepts: The interface through which one protocol consumes a lower service while preserving separate peer semantics and implementation state.

cards.definition: **Definition.** The maximum specified bit-transfer rate of one link under the named layer and coding boundary rather than an end-to-end completion rate.
major_error_concepts: Calling advertised line rate application goodput.
cards.prompt: Define Link bandwidth. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
required_concepts: The maximum specified bit-transfer rate of one link under the named layer and coding boundary rather than an end-to-end completion rate.

cards.definition: **Definition.** The separate absence late-order and repeated-delivery observations relative to a measured sequence and vantage.
major_error_concepts: Calling every gap loss immediately or every retransmission proof of original loss.
cards.prompt: Define Loss reorder and duplication state. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
required_concepts: The separate absence late-order and repeated-delivery observations relative to a measured sequence and vantage.

cards.definition: **Definition.** The interface direction clock capture mechanism sampling and visibility boundary governing what one trace can establish.
major_error_concepts: Treating one host capture as a complete path ground truth.
cards.prompt: Define Network observation vantage. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
required_concepts: The interface direction clock capture mechanism sampling and visibility boundary governing what one trace can establish.

cards.definition: **Definition.** The division of an application byte or message sequence into transport and network units under framing MTU and protocol rules.
major_error_concepts: Calling one application write one packet or one TCP segment permanently.
cards.prompt: Define Packetization boundary. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
required_concepts: The division of an application byte or message sequence into transport and network units under framing MTU and protocol rules.

cards.definition: **Definition.** The node-local interval for parsing lookup validation scheduling or protocol work under a configured implementation and load.
major_error_concepts: Calling all nonpropagation delay queueing.
cards.prompt: Define Processing delay. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
required_concepts: The node-local interval for parsing lookup validation scheduling or protocol work under a configured implementation and load.

cards.definition: **Definition.** The travel time implied by path length and signal propagation speed independent of packet length.
major_error_concepts: Using link bandwidth to compute propagation delay.
cards.prompt: Define Propagation delay. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
required_concepts: The travel time implied by path length and signal propagation speed independent of packet length.

cards.definition: **Definition.** The versioned message grammar endpoint roles state transitions timers errors extensibility rules and normative requirements governing peer communication.
major_error_concepts: Calling a port number or implementation name the protocol contract.
cards.prompt: Define Protocol contract. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
required_concepts: The versioned message grammar endpoint roles state transitions timers errors extensibility rules and normative requirements governing peer communication.

cards.definition: **Definition.** The version-qualified header fields and payload exchanged between peers at one layer with exact length and interpretation.
major_error_concepts: Calling every observed unit a packet and losing which protocol owns its fields.
cards.prompt: Define Protocol data unit. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
required_concepts: The version-qualified header fields and payload exchanged between peers at one layer with exact length and interpretation.

cards.definition: **Definition.** The waiting time before service at a bottleneck determined by arrival order queue state scheduler and service rate.
major_error_concepts: Using average utilization alone to claim an exact per-packet wait.
cards.prompt: Define Queueing delay. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
required_concepts: The waiting time before service at a bottleneck determined by arrival order queue state scheduler and service rate.

cards.definition: **Definition.** An observed-rate contract specifies the transferred quantity, successful-completion rule, observation interval, population, and direction used to compute a rate.
major_error_concepts: Dividing unlike quantities or measurements from different intervals and calling the result throughput.
cards.prompt: Define observed-rate contract. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
required_concepts: An observed-rate contract specifies the transferred quantity, successful-completion rule, observation interval, population, and direction used to compute a rate.

cards.definition: **Definition.** The time required to place a specified number of bits on a link at a configured line rate.
major_error_concepts: Dividing bytes by bits per second or including propagation distance twice.
cards.prompt: Define Serialization delay. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
required_concepts: The time required to place a specified number of bits on a link at a configured line rate.

cards.definition: **Definition.** The joined transmission propagation processing and queue timeline across specified hops and forwarding behavior.
major_error_concepts: Adding incompatible one-way RTT and per-link quantities or skipping repeated serialization.
cards.prompt: Define Store-and-forward path delay. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
required_concepts: The joined transmission propagation processing and queue timeline across specified hops and forwarding behavior.

cards.definition: **Definition.** The completed transferred bits or units divided by a declared observation interval population and direction.
major_error_concepts: Calling the smallest link rate observed throughput without a transfer measurement.
cards.prompt: Define Throughput. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
required_concepts: The completed transferred bits or units divided by a declared observation interval population and direction.

cards.definition: **Definition.** The time-qualified IPv4 protocol-to-link binding with origin reachability and expiry state used for local frame construction.
major_error_concepts: Calling cached ARP permanent authority or end-to-end reachability proof.
cards.prompt: Define ARP cache entry. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
required_concepts: The time-qualified IPv4 protocol-to-link binding with origin reachability and expiry state used for local frame construction.

cards.definition: **Definition.** The IPv4 local-link exchange asking for a protocol-address binding and returning a claimed link address under cache and trust qualifications.
major_error_concepts: Sending ARP to a remote subnet host rather than the next hop.
cards.prompt: Define ARP request and reply. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
required_concepts: The IPv4 local-link exchange asking for a protocol-address binding and returning a claimed link address under cache and trust qualifications.

cards.definition: **Definition.** The set of interfaces receiving a specified link broadcast absent filtering segmentation or routing boundaries.
major_error_concepts: Calling every switched network one broadcast domain regardless of segmentation.
cards.prompt: Define Broadcast domain. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
required_concepts: The set of interfaces receiving a specified link broadcast absent filtering segmentation or routing boundaries.

cards.definition: **Definition.** The frame-delivery distinction between one link destination and all members of a broadcast domain under switch behavior.
major_error_concepts: Forwarding a link broadcast through routers by default.
cards.prompt: Define Ethernet unicast and broadcast scope. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
required_concepts: The frame-delivery distinction between one link destination and all members of a broadcast domain under switch behavior.

cards.definition: **Definition.** An IPv6 Neighbor Discovery message is an ICMPv6 control message interpreted under Neighbor Discovery type, code, option, source, destination, hop-limit, and link-scope validation rules.
major_error_concepts: Interpreting an ICMPv6 type without enforcing Neighbor Discovery link-scope and message-validation rules.
cards.prompt: Define IPv6 Neighbor Discovery message. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
required_concepts: An IPv6 Neighbor Discovery message is an ICMPv6 control message interpreted under Neighbor Discovery type, code, option, source, destination, hop-limit, and link-scope validation rules.

cards.definition: An IPv6 solicited-node multicast address is the link-local multicast address obtained by appending the target unicast or anycast address low-order 24 bits to ff02::1:ff00:0/104. Neighbor Solicitation uses the corresponding group for address resolution, rather than an IPv4-style broadcast. Different addresses sharing those low bits share the group, so group membership is not a unique host identity.
major_error_concepts: Using all target bits as an IPv6 broadcast destination.
Assuming different IPv6 addresses always have different solicited-node multicast groups.
cards.prompt: Define IPv6 solicited-node multicast. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
required_concepts: Construct the address from ff02::1:ff00:0/104 plus the target low 24 bits.
It narrows on-link solicitation scope but is not broadcast or a globally unique host identifier.

cards.definition: **Definition.** The time-qualified mapping from observed source link addresses to ingress ports used for later forwarding decisions.
major_error_concepts: Learning destinations from destination fields or keeping stale movement forever.
cards.prompt: Define Learning-switch table. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
required_concepts: The time-qualified mapping from observed source link addresses to ingress ports used for later forwarding decisions.

cards.definition: **Definition.** The local-link identifier used for delivery on one link and resolved or configured under that link protocol.
major_error_concepts: Treating a MAC-like value as global host identity.
cards.prompt: Define Link address. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
required_concepts: The local-link identifier used for delivery on one link and resolved or configured under that link protocol.

cards.definition: **Definition.** The link-local corruption-detection field and validation boundary that can reject a frame without providing end-to-end correctness.
major_error_concepts: Calling a valid link check proof that transport or application bytes are correct everywhere.
cards.prompt: Define Link integrity check. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
required_concepts: The link-local corruption-detection field and validation boundary that can reject a frame without providing end-to-end correctness.

cards.definition: **Definition.** The local-link protocol unit carrying addressing type length integrity and payload fields under one link contract.
major_error_concepts: Using final remote host link address across routed hops.
cards.prompt: Define Link-layer frame. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
required_concepts: The local-link protocol unit carrying addressing type length integrity and payload fields under one link contract.

cards.definition: **Definition.** The maximum network-layer unit accepted on one interface under a configured link configuration and encapsulation.
major_error_concepts: Subtracting Ethernet-visible frame header from an already stated IP MTU twice.
cards.prompt: Define Link MTU. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
required_concepts: The maximum network-layer unit accepted on one interface under a configured link configuration and encapsulation.

cards.definition: **Definition.** The IPv6 response or announcement carrying target and link information with solicited override and router flags affecting cache state.
major_error_concepts: Calling every advertisement authoritative or equivalent to a router advertisement.
cards.prompt: Define Neighbor Advertisement. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
required_concepts: The IPv6 response or announcement carrying target and link information with solicited override and router flags affecting cache state.

cards.definition: RFC 4861 neighbor-cache reachability uses five conceptual states: INCOMPLETE (address resolution pending), REACHABLE (recent positive confirmation), STALE (confirmation expired), DELAY (briefly waiting for upper-layer confirmation after use), and PROBE (sending unicast reachability probes). STALE does not mean the cached address is unusable. After probe failure the conceptual entry is discarded; implementations may expose extra labels such as FAILED, which should be identified as local extensions.
major_error_concepts: Treating STALE as an unusable mapping that cannot be used to send a packet.
Claiming FAILED is a sixth mandatory state in the RFC 4861 conceptual machine.
cards.prompt: Define Neighbor-cache reachability state. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
required_concepts: Distinguish the five RFC states INCOMPLETE, REACHABLE, STALE, DELAY and PROBE and their reachability/resolution roles.
STALE remains usable while reachability is checked; extra implementation failure labels are not additional required RFC states.

cards.definition: **Definition.** The IPv6 Neighbor Discovery message used for address resolution reachability or duplicate-address contexts with source and target rules.
major_error_concepts: Using it to query arbitrary off-link addresses directly.
cards.prompt: Define Neighbor Solicitation. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
required_concepts: The IPv6 Neighbor Discovery message used for address resolution reachability or duplicate-address contexts with source and target rules.

cards.definition: **Definition.** The host or router attachment with link protocol addresses MTU operational state queues and counters under one observation boundary.
major_error_concepts: Calling an interface a permanent physical port or one IP address.
cards.prompt: Define Network interface. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
required_concepts: The host or router attachment with link protocol addresses MTU operational state queues and counters under one observation boundary.

cards.definition: **Definition.** The forwarding decision that retains the remote network destination while addressing the local frame to an on-link gateway.
major_error_concepts: Replacing destination IP with gateway IP in the forwarded packet.
cards.prompt: Define Off-link next-hop delivery. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
required_concepts: The forwarding decision that retains the remote network destination while addressing the local frame to an on-link gateway.

cards.definition: **Definition.** The IPv6 host-router messages supplying default-router prefix and configuration context separately from neighbor address resolution.
major_error_concepts: Calling router advertisement a DNS answer or universal authenticated configuration.
cards.prompt: Define Router Solicitation and Advertisement. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
required_concepts: The IPv6 host-router messages supplying default-router prefix and configuration context separately from neighbor address resolution.

cards.definition: **Definition.** The local replication of a frame when the switch lacks a usable destination entry with ingress exclusion and scope rules.
major_error_concepts: Calling flooding routing or proof that every recipient accepts the payload.
cards.prompt: Define Unknown-unicast flooding. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
required_concepts: The local replication of a frame when the switch lacks a usable destination entry with ingress exclusion and scope rules.

cards.definition: **Definition.** The protocol-visible loss delay rate and retransmission variation on a wireless hop without claiming physical-layer cause.
major_error_concepts: Inferring interference source or channel capacity from one application slowdown.
cards.prompt: Define Wireless-link variability boundary. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
required_concepts: The protocol-visible loss delay rate and retransmission variation on a wireless hop without claiming physical-layer cause.

cards.definition: **Definition.** The replacement of contiguous aligned more-specific prefixes by a covering prefix only when routing and policy permit the broader advertisement.
major_error_concepts: Combining nonaligned ranges or assuming reachability for every address in the cover.
cards.prompt: Define CIDR aggregation. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
required_concepts: The replacement of contiguous aligned more-specific prefixes by a covering prefix only when routing and policy permit the broader advertisement.

cards.definition: **Definition.** The data-plane operation applying selected route interface next hop header updates MTU and policy results to one packet.
major_error_concepts: Treating control-plane topology as the packet's direct forwarding instructions.
cards.prompt: Define Forwarding-table action. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
required_concepts: The data-plane operation applying selected route interface next hop header updates MTU and policy results to one packet.

cards.definition: **Definition.** The versioned error message containing enough invoking-packet context to associate a network failure with a flow while obeying generation limits.
major_error_concepts: Treating an ICMP source address as proof of the exact failed link.
cards.prompt: Define ICMP error quotation. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
required_concepts: The versioned error message containing enough invoking-packet context to associate a network failure with a flow while obeying generation limits.

cards.definition: **Definition.** The error generated for hop-limit exhaustion or reassembly timeout under version-specific rules and observation limits.
major_error_concepts: Calling no reply proof that no router exists at that hop.
cards.prompt: Define ICMP time exceeded. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
required_concepts: The error generated for hop-limit exhaustion or reassembly timeout under version-specific rules and observation limits.

cards.definition: **Definition.** The 32-bit address plus prefix-length set membership used for interface and route context without classful assumptions.
major_error_concepts: Using dotted-decimal visual similarity instead of prefix bits.
cards.prompt: Define IPv4 address and prefix. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
required_concepts: The 32-bit address plus prefix-length set membership used for interface and route context without classful assumptions.

cards.definition: **Definition.** The version-specific division of a datagram into offset-aligned fragments with identification flags and destination reassembly under MTU constraints.
major_error_concepts: Splitting total bytes evenly without header or eight-byte offset rules.
cards.prompt: Define IPv4 fragmentation. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
required_concepts: The version-specific division of a datagram into offset-aligned fragments with identification flags and destination reassembly under MTU constraints.

cards.definition: **Definition.** The one's-complement integrity check over the IPv4 header that routers update when mutable header fields change.
major_error_concepts: Calling it an end-to-end payload checksum or applying it to IPv6.
cards.prompt: Define IPv4 header checksum. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
required_concepts: The one's-complement integrity check over the IPv4 header that routers update when mutable header fields change.

cards.definition: **Definition.** The exact address set represented by one prefix with host-use qualifications separated from mathematical membership.
major_error_concepts: Subtracting two hosts universally or calling the prefix a single interface.
cards.prompt: Define IPv4 subnet range. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
required_concepts: The exact address set represented by one prefix with host-use qualifications separated from mathematical membership.

cards.definition: **Definition.** The 128-bit address and prefix set with compression syntax separated from actual bits and scope.
major_error_concepts: Treating omitted zero groups as variable-length bits or applying IPv4 broadcast rules.
cards.prompt: Define IPv6 address and prefix. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
required_concepts: The 128-bit address and prefix set with compression syntax separated from actual bits and scope.

cards.definition: **Definition.** The endpoint use of a Fragment extension header while routers do not fragment ordinary forwarded IPv6 packets.
major_error_concepts: Having an IPv6 router fragment the packet like IPv4.
cards.prompt: Define IPv6 source fragmentation. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
required_concepts: The endpoint use of a Fragment extension header while routers do not fragment ordinary forwarded IPv6 packets.

cards.definition: **Definition.** The forwarding selection of the matching destination prefix with greatest length before later tie-breaking.
major_error_concepts: Choosing the lowest metric before comparing prefix specificity.
cards.prompt: Define Longest-prefix match. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
required_concepts: The forwarding selection of the matching destination prefix with greatest length before later tie-breaking.

cards.definition: **Definition.** The middlebox translation between internal and external endpoint tuples with direction timers and filtering behavior under one implementation.
major_error_concepts: Calling NAT stateless address substitution or proof of authorization.
cards.prompt: Define NAT mapping state. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
required_concepts: The middlebox translation between internal and external endpoint tuples with direction timers and filtering behavior under one implementation.

cards.definition: **Definition.** The ICMP signal carrying a constraining MTU so an endpoint can adjust packet size under validation and state rules.
major_error_concepts: Accepting arbitrary unauthenticated MTU values forever or changing link MTU itself.
cards.prompt: Define Packet-too-big feedback. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
required_concepts: The ICMP signal carrying a constraining MTU so an endpoint can adjust packet size under validation and state rules.

cards.definition: **Definition.** The endpoint's time-qualified bound on packet size along a path and protocol context inferred from messages probes and loss behavior.
major_error_concepts: Calling one probe result the permanent minimum MTU for a destination host.
cards.prompt: Define Path-MTU estimate. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
required_concepts: The endpoint's time-qualified bound on packet size along a path and protocol context inferred from messages probes and loss behavior.

cards.definition: **Definition.** The designated non-global IPv4 address space whose routing treatment and uniqueness are local-policy matters.
major_error_concepts: Calling private addresses encrypted secure or globally unique.
cards.prompt: Define Private-address scope. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
required_concepts: The designated non-global IPv4 address space whose routing treatment and uniqueness are local-policy matters.

cards.definition: **Definition.** The lookup required when a route names a gateway whose own on-link reachability must be established without infinite recursion.
major_error_concepts: Sending a frame to a gateway not known to be on link.
cards.prompt: Define Recursive next-hop resolution. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
required_concepts: The lookup required when a route names a gateway whose own on-link reachability must be established without infinite recursion.

cards.definition: **Definition.** The destination prefix next-hop or direct-delivery action outgoing interface metric source preference and lifecycle state considered by forwarding.
major_error_concepts: Calling an advertised route an installed route or a route proof of path success.
cards.prompt: Define Route entry. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
required_concepts: The destination prefix next-hop or direct-delivery action outgoing interface metric source preference and lifecycle state considered by forwarding.

cards.definition: **Definition.** The per-forwarding-node decrement preventing indefinite circulation and triggering version-specific discard and error behavior at exhaustion.
major_error_concepts: Decrementing at end hosts only or forwarding with zero.
cards.prompt: Define TTL and hop-limit transition. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
required_concepts: The per-forwarding-node decrement preventing indefinite circulation and triggering version-specific discard and error behavior at exhaustion.

cards.definition: **Definition.** The routing-policy domain identified for interdomain exchange without implying one organization topology or trust boundary universally.
major_error_concepts: Calling an AS one router or one guaranteed legal organization.
cards.prompt: Define Autonomous system. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
required_concepts: The routing-policy domain identified for interdomain exchange without implying one organization topology or trust boundary universally.

cards.definition: **Definition.** The local minimization over neighbor cost plus advertised destination estimate under a recorded message round.
major_error_concepts: Adding A's stale destination estimate twice or mixing rounds.
cards.prompt: Define Bellman-Ford routing update. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
required_concepts: The local minimization over neighbor cost plus advertised destination estimate under a recorded message round.

cards.definition: **Definition.** The versioned origin AS path next hop preference and other properties carried or assigned for route selection and policy.
major_error_concepts: Choosing the shortest AS path before a higher-priority local policy.
cards.prompt: Define BGP path attributes. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
required_concepts: The versioned origin AS path next hop preference and other properties carried or assigned for route selection and policy.

cards.definition: **Definition.** The local choice among accepted paths and neighbor-specific announcement rules reflecting relationships and safety constraints.
major_error_concepts: Advertising every selected route to every peer or calling policy global optimality.
cards.prompt: Define BGP selection and export policy. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
required_concepts: The local choice among accepted paths and neighbor-specific announcement rules reflecting relationships and safety constraints.

cards.definition: **Definition.** The eBGP or iBGP relationship carrying path-vector information under transport policy and propagation rules.
major_error_concepts: Calling iBGP an intradomain shortest-path protocol.
cards.prompt: Define BGP session role. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
required_concepts: The eBGP or iBGP relationship carrying path-vector information under transport policy and propagation rules.

cards.definition: **Definition.** The incremental advertisement or removal of reachable prefixes and path attributes over an established session.
major_error_concepts: Treating session liveness as proof every earlier route remains valid.
cards.prompt: Define BGP update and withdrawal. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
required_concepts: The incremental advertisement or removal of reachable prefixes and path attributes over an established session.

cards.definition: **Definition.** The gradual increase of distance-vector estimates for an unreachable destination under limited local knowledge.
major_error_concepts: Jumping immediately to infinity while claiming the trace demonstrates count to infinity.
cards.prompt: Define Count-to-infinity behavior. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
required_concepts: The gradual increase of distance-vector estimates for an unreachable destination under limited local knowledge.

cards.definition: **Definition.** The per-destination local cost and next-hop estimates learned through neighbors rather than a complete topology map.
major_error_concepts: Giving every node the global graph while calling it distance vector.
cards.prompt: Define Distance-vector state. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
required_concepts: The per-destination local cost and next-hop estimates learned through neighbors rather than a complete topology map.

cards.definition: **Definition.** The versioned statement of one router's adjacencies or network links with sequence age scope and flooding behavior.
major_error_concepts: Calling one received advertisement the complete current topology.
cards.prompt: Define Link-state advertisement. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
required_concepts: The versioned statement of one router's adjacencies or network links with sequence age scope and flooding behavior.

cards.definition: **Definition.** The router's time-qualified collection of accepted advertisements from which a topology view is constructed.
major_error_concepts: Assuming all routers update atomically.
cards.prompt: Define Link-state database. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
required_concepts: The router's time-qualified collection of accepted advertisements from which a topology view is constructed.

cards.definition: **Definition.** The specified vertices links directions capacities or costs and failure state over which one routing algorithm reasons.
major_error_concepts: Drawing a logical link and assuming bidirectional equal cost or current liveness.
cards.prompt: Define Network topology graph. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
required_concepts: The specified vertices links directions capacities or costs and failure state over which one routing algorithm reasons.

cards.definition: **Definition.** The introductory neighbor state and database-exchange relationship required before routing information is fully synchronized.
major_error_concepts: Calling receipt of one hello a full synchronized adjacency.
cards.prompt: Define OSPF adjacency context. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
required_concepts: The introductory neighbor state and database-exchange relationship required before routing information is fully synchronized.

cards.definition: **Definition.** The introductory derivation of intra-area routes from an accepted link-state database and local interface state.
major_error_concepts: Applying BGP policy attributes inside the OSPF shortest-path calculation.
cards.prompt: Define OSPF route calculation. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
required_concepts: The introductory derivation of intra-area routes from an accepted link-state database and local interface state.

cards.definition: **Definition.** The distinction between learning or selecting paths and applying installed data-plane actions to packets.
major_error_concepts: Calling a routing update proof that the next packet takes that path.

cards.definition: In distance-vector routing, simple split horizon omits a route from advertisements back toward the neighbor or interface from which that route was learned. Split horizon with poisoned reverse advertises that route back with an unreachable/infinite metric instead. This avoids selected two-router feedback loops, but does not establish universal loop freedom or immediate convergence; larger loops can remain.
major_error_concepts: Reversing which strategy omits the route and which advertises an unreachable metric.
Claiming either rule proves all distance-vector loops impossible.
cards.prompt: Define Split horizon and poison reverse. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
required_concepts: Split horizon suppresses the learned route back toward its source; poisoned reverse instead advertises it there as unreachable.
The mitigation is neighbor/interface-specific and does not eliminate all larger loops or convergence delay.

required_concepts: The circular next-hop state during asynchronous convergence that can forward packets repeatedly until hop limit expires.

cards.definition: Under RFC 6298, a TCP retransmission timeout is computed as RTO=SRTT+max(G,4*RTTVAR), with clock granularity G; the RFC recommends rounding computed values below one second up to one second. Before an RTT sample, it recommends an initial RTO of one second or a more conservative value. A retransmission timeout backs the timer off by doubling RTO, subject to the specified bounds. Expiration triggers recovery but does not prove the receiver received no data: an ACK may have been delayed or lost.
major_error_concepts: Setting RTO equal to SRTT while ignoring variation and granularity.
Treating timeout as certain evidence that the receiver observed no bytes.
cards.prompt: Under RFC 6298, how is TCP RTO computed and backed off, and what does expiration fail to prove?
required_concepts: State RTO=SRTT+max(G,4*RTTVAR) with the specified granularity and RFC floor policy.
Timeout recovery includes exponential backoff, and a timeout is not proof of data nonarrival.

cards.definition: For the first valid RTT sample R, RFC 6298 initializes SRTT=R and RTTVAR=R/2. For a later valid sample Rnew, first set RTTVAR=(1-beta)*old_RTTVAR+beta*abs(old_SRTT-Rnew), then SRTT=(1-alpha)*old_SRTT+alpha*Rnew, with recommended alpha=1/8 and beta=1/4. The variation update uses the old SRTT, not its newly updated value. Samples must satisfy the RTT-measurement rules, including avoiding ambiguous retransmission samples unless the ambiguity is resolved.
major_error_concepts: Updating SRTT first and then using the new SRTT in the variation residual.
Using an unqualified RTT sample from an ambiguously retransmitted segment.
cards.prompt: Give the RFC 6298 SRTT/RTTVAR initialization and subsequent update equations, including which SRTT appears in the variation residual.
required_concepts: First sample initializes SRTT=R and RTTVAR=R/2.
Later updates use beta=1/4 on absolute deviation from old SRTT and alpha=1/8 on SRTT; preserve the stated update order and valid-sample condition.

cards.definition: **Definition.** TLS 1.3 record protection uses direction-specific AEAD keys, per-record nonces, sequence state, authenticated record metadata, and strict failure handling to protect application and handshake fragments.
major_error_concepts: Treating encryption without authentication, sequence state, or fatal failure handling as equivalent record protection.
cards.prompt: Define TLS 1.3 record protection. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
required_concepts: TLS 1.3 record protection uses direction-specific AEAD keys, per-record nonces, sequence state, authenticated record metadata, and strict failure handling to protect application and handshake fragments.

cards.definition: **Definition.** Server Name Indication is a ClientHello extension conveying the intended server name so a multi-tenant endpoint can select configuration and credentials; in ordinary TLS 1.3 it is not encrypted from on-path observers.
major_error_concepts: Treating SNI as certificate hostname validation or as confidential by default.
cards.prompt: Define TLS Server Name Indication. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
required_concepts: Server Name Indication is a ClientHello extension conveying the intended server name so a multi-tenant endpoint can select configuration and credentials; in ordinary TLS 1.3 it is not encrypted from on-path observers.

cards.definition: **Definition.** TLS server-name validation checks that the authenticated certificate identity matches the intended reference hostname under the applicable name-matching rules.
major_error_concepts: Validating a chain but not the intended hostname and therefore authenticating the wrong endpoint.
cards.prompt: Define TLS server-name validation. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
required_concepts: TLS server-name validation checks that the authenticated certificate identity matches the intended reference hostname under the applicable name-matching rules.

cards.definition: **Definition.** TLS 1.3 session resumption uses a resumption secret and server-issued ticket or pre-shared-key identity to authenticate a later handshake under bounded lifetime, policy, and key-compromise assumptions.
major_error_concepts: Calling resumption a continuation of the same transport connection or assuming it preserves every property of a fresh certificate-authenticated handshake.
cards.prompt: Define TLS 1.3 session resumption. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
required_concepts: TLS 1.3 session resumption uses a resumption secret and server-issued ticket or pre-shared-key identity to authenticate a later handshake under bounded lifetime, policy, and key-compromise assumptions.

cards.definition: **Definition.** A TLS traffic secret is a direction- and epoch-specific secret from which record-protection keys and initialization vectors are derived and later updated independently by each sender.
major_error_concepts: Reusing one traffic key across directions or after a key-update boundary.
cards.prompt: Define TLS traffic secret. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
required_concepts: A TLS traffic secret is a direction- and epoch-specific secret from which record-protection keys and initialization vectors are derived and later updated independently by each sender.

cards.definition: **Definition.** TLS 0-RTT early data can reduce latency during resumption but lacks ordinary handshake replay protection, so applications must restrict it to operations safe under possible replay and server acceptance races.
major_error_concepts: Sending non-idempotent or authority-changing operations as early data and relying on TLS to make replay impossible.
cards.prompt: What boundary or limitation does TLS 0-RTT replay boundary impose?
required_concepts: TLS 0-RTT early data can reduce latency during resumption but lacks ordinary handshake replay protection, so applications must restrict it to operations safe under possible replay and server acceptance races.

required_concepts: The controlled exchange between independent implementations across versions options and failures with exact artifacts and observations.

required_concepts: The localization of version negotiation certificate authentication transcript alert resumption or application handoff failure.

cards.definition: **Definition.** The valid address-multiple constraint for an object type under the target ABI and allocation interface.

cards.prompt: Define Alignment requirement. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
required_concepts: The valid address-multiple constraint for an object type under the target ABI and allocation interface.

cards.definition: In C11 terminology, specified behavior is determined by the standard for the stated case. Implementation-defined behavior allows documented implementation choices. Unspecified behavior allows a set of alternatives without requiring the implementation to document which is chosen. Undefined behavior imposes no requirements on that execution. A debugger observation does not turn an unspecified choice or undefined execution into a portable guarantee.
major_error_concepts: Treating undefined behavior as a guaranteed implementation-specific result.
Saying unspecified behavior requires a documented implementation choice.
cards.prompt: In C11, distinguish specified, implementation-defined, unspecified and undefined behavior.
required_concepts: Distinguish a standard-prescribed result, documented implementation choice, undocumented permitted alternatives, and undefined behavior with no requirements.
An observed result alone does not establish a portable language guarantee.

cards.definition: **Definition.** The exact positional encodings of one finite-width bit vector with leading zeros preserved when width matters.
major_error_concepts: Dropping leading zeros then inferring a different sign or object size.
cards.prompt: Define Binary and hexadecimal notation. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
required_concepts: The exact positional encodings of one finite-width bit vector with leading zeros preserved when width matters.

cards.definition: **Definition.** The distinction between a binary digit a minimum addressable byte and the implementation-defined number of bits represented by CHAR_BIT.

cards.prompt: Define Bit and byte identity. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
required_concepts: The distinction between a binary digit a minimum addressable byte and the implementation-defined number of bits represented by CHAR_BIT.

required_concepts: The finite-width application of AND OR XOR or complement to corresponding bits after operand conversions.

required_concepts: The target mapping of multibyte object-representation significance to increasing byte addresses.

cards.prompt: Define C object. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
required_concepts: A region of data storage whose type lifetime value and object representation are governed separately from the expression naming it.

cards.prompt: Define Floating-point exceptional class. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.

cards.prompt: Define Floating-point rounding. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
required_concepts: The mapping of an exact real result to a representable value under a named rounding mode with precision and exceptional status.

cards.prompt: Define Integer conversion rank. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
required_concepts: The language ordering used with promotions and usual arithmetic conversions to choose operand types before an operation.

cards.prompt: Define ABI argument passage. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.

cards.prompt: Define ABI return value. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
required_concepts: The convention for returning scalar aggregate or hidden-address results with exact type classification.

required_concepts: The arithmetic combination of base index scale displacement and instruction context used to select memory without itself dereferencing.

required_concepts: The ISA-defined byte sequence selecting opcode operand forms widths and addressing information at one program address.

required_concepts: The immediate register or memory value consumed or produced by an instruction with size and address fixed.

cards.definition: A dangling pointer is a pointer associated with an object whose lifetime has ended, for example after deallocation or exit from the owning automatic-storage scope. It no longer provides valid access to that former object. In C11, such a pointer value becomes indeterminate; a remembered address or a non-null test is not a lifetime guarantee. Keeping an alias does not keep the object alive.
major_error_concepts: Defining dangling as merely having a null address.
Assuming an old alias keeps freed or out-of-scope storage alive.
cards.prompt: Define Dangling pointer. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
required_concepts: The referenced object lifetime has ended, so the old reference no longer authorizes object access.
A retained alias or apparently non-null address does not restore the object lifetime.

cards.definition: A double free attempts to deallocate an allocation that has already been deallocated, without a new valid allocation ownership contract. In C, a repeated free of that allocation is undefined behavior; free(NULL) is a permitted no-op. A later fresh allocation may reuse an address without being the same allocation identity. Nulling one alias does not repair other stale aliases.
major_error_concepts: Calling repeated free(NULL) a double-free violation.
Freeing through a stale alias after another alias released the allocation.
cards.prompt: Define Double free. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
required_concepts: The same allocation has already been freed; distinguish allocation identity from a reusable numeric address.
free(NULL) is a no-op, and stale aliases still require correct lifetime/ownership handling.

cards.definition: **Definition.** The language rules governing which lvalue types may access stored object representations with character-type exceptions and allocated-storage qualifications.
major_error_concepts: Assuming same size makes two pointer casts safely dereferenceable.
cards.prompt: Define Effective type and aliasing. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
required_concepts: The language rules governing which lvalue types may access stored object representations with character-type exceptions and allocated-storage qualifications.

major_error_concepts: Calling all memory retained until process exit harmless regardless of loop or service lifetime.
cards.prompt: Define Memory leak. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
required_concepts: The loss of every usable ownership path to a live resource before its required release under the program contract.

cards.prompt: Define Null pointer. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
required_concepts: The distinguished pointer value comparing unequal to every valid object or function pointer with representation not assumed all-zero bytes universally.

cards.prompt: Define Out-of-bounds access. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
required_concepts: The attempted lvalue evaluation or memory operation outside a live object's permitted elements and one-past formation rules.

cards.prompt: Define Pointer alias. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
required_concepts: Pointer aliases are two expressions that may designate overlapping storage, with consequences for updates and compiler reasoning.

cards.definition: For C11 array-pointer arithmetic, adding or subtracting an integer moves by elements, not raw bytes, and must stay within the same array object or its one-past position. Subtracting pointers in that array gives an element difference when representable in ptrdiff_t. A one-past pointer is not dereferenceable. Pointer equality is a separate operation that may compare valid pointers to different objects; arithmetic and relational ordering have stricter object-context rules.
major_error_concepts: Forming arbitrary out-of-array pointers and assuming only dereference is restricted.
Claiming equality comparison of two valid unrelated object pointers is automatically undefined.
cards.prompt: What are the C11 array-pointer arithmetic rules, and how do they differ from pointer equality?
required_concepts: Pointer offsets count elements and remain inside the array or one-past; same-array pointer subtraction yields a representable element difference.
One-past may not be dereferenced; do not confuse arithmetic/relational restrictions with pointer equality.

cards.definition: **Definition.** The pointer whose referent is an entire fixed-shape array and whose arithmetic advances by whole rows.

cards.prompt: Define Pointer-to-array type. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
required_concepts: The pointer whose referent is an entire fixed-shape array and whose arithmetic advances by whole rows.

major_error_concepts: Treating any integer equal to an address as an interchangeable valid pointer.

required_concepts: The typed value designating an object function one-past position or null under language rules rather than merely a numeric address.

cards.prompt: Define Structure member address. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
required_concepts: The target layout mapping from structure base through member offsets and alignment to subobject addresses.

cards.definition: **Definition.** The access to an object or padding whose value has not been established with indeterminate and trap qualifications.

cards.prompt: Define Uninitialized read. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.

cards.definition: For POSIX-style regular-file reads, a nonnegative return value is the number of bytes actually read; it can be shorter than requested. For a positive request size, zero indicates the file position is at or beyond EOF at that time. A request for zero bytes can return zero without proving EOF. On error, read returns -1 with errno; process only the returned byte count and handle EINTR or would-block errors according to their contract. Other descriptor types can have additional zero-return semantics.
major_error_concepts: Treating a zero-byte read result as proof the file has no more data.
Using all requested buffer bytes after only a short count was returned.
cards.prompt: For POSIX-style regular-file read calls, interpret full/short, zero and error results, including a zero-byte request.
required_concepts: Interpret positive/short byte counts as actual progress and -1 with errno as error, not a full-buffer guarantee.
Zero indicates EOF for the specified positive-count regular-file case, but a zero-length request returning zero is not EOF evidence.
