cards.definition: **Definition.** One checker-emitted severity, code, message, source location, related context, and configuration-sensitive judgment tied to a recorded analysis without itself proving a runtime defect.
major_error_concepts: Treating every diagnostic as a demonstrated runtime crash or every warning as optional noise.
cards.prompt: Define Static-checker diagnostic. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
required_concepts: A static-checker diagnostic is emitted by one recorded checker analysis.
The diagnostic records severity.
The diagnostic records an error code when the checker supplies one.
The diagnostic records the full message.
The diagnostic records the source location.
The diagnostic records related context.
The diagnostic is a configuration-sensitive static judgment.
A static-checker diagnostic does not by itself prove a runtime defect.

cards.definition:
**Definition.** A versioned checker identifier classifying one family of static judgments for configuration, suppression, documentation lookup, and longitudinal comparison while retaining the full message and context.

**Worked check.** Record `mypy` code `arg-type` with file and line; suppressing every diagnostic on that line is broader than a targeted `# type: ignore[arg-type]`.
major_error_concepts: Treating a stable-looking code as checker-independent or semantically identical across versions.
cards.prompt: What does Checker error code diagnose or distinguish?
required_concepts: A checker error code is a versioned checker identifier.
The code classifies one family of static judgments.
The code can participate in checker configuration.
The code can target a suppression.
The code can anchor documentation lookup and longitudinal comparison.
The diagnostic's full message and context remain necessary evidence alongside the code.

cards.definition: **Definition.** The version-bound relation the checker derives between filesystem paths and qualified module names using roots, package markers, namespace settings, explicit bases, and target selection.
major_error_concepts: Assuming checker module identity always matches a filename relative to the shell directory.
cards.prompt: Define Checker file-to-module mapping. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
required_concepts: Checker file-to-module mapping relates filesystem paths to qualified module names.
The mapping is bound to a checker version.
The checker derives the mapping from configured roots and package markers.
The checker applies configured namespace-package settings.
The checker applies explicit module bases when configured.
Target selection participates in the resulting mapping.

cards.definition: **Definition.** The effective rules deciding whether imported modules are located, analyzed, skipped, silenced, or represented through stubs or `Any`, with per-module overrides and missing-import behavior explicit.
major_error_concepts: Treating lack of import diagnostics as proof every dependency was fully typed and analyzed.
cards.prompt: Define Checker import-following policy. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
required_concepts: A checker import-following policy determines whether imported modules are located and analyzed.
The policy may instead skip, silence, stub, or represent an imported module through `Any`.
The effective policy includes per-module overrides.
The effective policy states how missing imports are handled.

cards.definition: **Definition.** The specified command, working directory, environment, arguments, explicit targets, discovered configuration, cache mode, stdout, stderr, and exit status used to start one checker run.
major_error_concepts: Recording only the command name while target selection and configuration discovery remain implicit.
cards.prompt: Define Type-checker invocation. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
required_concepts: A type-checker invocation records the command used to start the run.
The invocation records the working directory.
The invocation records relevant environment values.
The invocation records command arguments.
The invocation records explicit targets.
The invocation records the configuration discovered by the checker.
The invocation records the cache mode.
The invocation records standard output and standard error.
The invocation records the checker process's exit status.

cards.definition: **Definition.** The recorded invocation, effective configuration, denominator, diagnostics by severity and code, suppressions, internal failures, stdout, stderr, duration, cache state, and exit status for one completed analysis.
major_error_concepts: Calling exit status zero a clean full-project analysis without denominator and suppression evidence.
cards.prompt: Define Type-checker run result. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
required_concepts: A type-checker run result records the exact invocation.
The result records the effective configuration.
The result records the checked-file denominator.
The result groups diagnostics by severity and code.
The result records active suppressions.
The result records checker-internal failures.
The result records standard output and standard error.
The result records run duration.
The result records cache state.
The result records process exit status.
All fields refer to one completed analysis.

cards.definition: **Definition.** A type-checker target Python version is the configured language version and platform against which syntax, standard-library types, conditional definitions, and version-sensitive typing features are interpreted.
major_error_concepts: Assuming the interpreter running a checker is automatically the language version targeted by the analysis.
cards.prompt: Define type-checker target Python version. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
required_concepts: A type-checker target records the configured Python language version.
A type-checker target records the configured platform.
The checker interprets syntax against that target.
The checker interprets standard-library types against that target.
The checker interprets conditional definitions against that target.
The checker interprets version-sensitive typing features against that target.

accepted_variants: a is present in the cache but X is absent, so the direct read raises AttributeError. Put the shared definition in module c, or explicitly defer access until initialization is complete and check the resulting execution paths.
cards.definition: a is cached but only partially initialized; X has not yet been assigned. Ordinary a.X access raises AttributeError. Break the dependency cycle by moving shared definitions into a third module, or defer the read until initialization has completed with the resulting lifecycle explicitly controlled. Reordering imports alone is not a general repair.
major_error_concepts: Because a is in sys.modules, X is already available; changing import order always eliminates the underlying dependency cycle.
cards.prompt: Assume fresh ordinary modules: a imports b before assigning X; b imports a and reads a.X during b's initialization. What happens at that read, and how can the design avoid reliance on accidental import ordering?
required_concepts: At the read, a exists as a partially initialized module but lacks X; ordinary attribute lookup fails.
Give a repair that removes or controls the early-read dependency rather than relying on a different accidental startup order.

cards.definition: **Definition.** A name-to-object binding stored on a class or ancestor namespace and potentially visible through instances unless shadowed or transformed by descriptor behavior.
major_error_concepts: Calling a value class-level merely because it is read with `instance.name`.
cards.prompt: Define Class attribute. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
required_concepts: A class attribute is a name-to-object binding stored on a class or ancestor namespace.
The binding can be visible through instances.
Instance shadowing or descriptor behavior can change the value observed through an instance.

cards.definition: **Definition.** A descriptor-mediated method whose implicit first argument is the accessing class, supporting class-aware alternate construction or behavior while remaining subject to inheritance binding.
major_error_concepts: Calling it a static utility merely because it can be accessed on the class.
cards.prompt: Define Class method. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
required_concepts: A class method is mediated by a descriptor.
A class method receives the accessing class as its implicit first argument.
A class method can implement class-aware alternate construction or behavior.
Class-method binding remains subject to inheritance and the accessing class identity.

cards.definition: **Definition.** The runtime object created by class definition machinery that carries attributes, participates in instance construction and inheritance, and is itself distinct from every instance it creates.
major_error_concepts: Treating a class as only a template with no runtime identity or mutable state.
cards.prompt: Define Python class object. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
required_concepts: A Python class object is a runtime object created by class-definition machinery.
The class object carries class attributes.
The class object participates in instance construction.
The class object participates in inheritance relations.
The class object is distinct from every instance it creates.

cards.definition: **Definition.** A typing annotation marking a class-level variable rather than an instance field for checker and dataclass interpretation, without preventing runtime instance shadowing through ordinary Python mechanisms.
major_error_concepts: Assuming `ClassVar` creates enforced and read-only runtime class storage.
cards.prompt: Define Static `ClassVar` annotation. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
required_concepts: A static `ClassVar` annotation marks a variable as class-level rather than an instance field.
Compatible checkers and dataclass processing use that distinction.
`ClassVar` does not prevent runtime instance shadowing through ordinary Python mechanisms.

cards.definition: **Definition.** The specified discovery roots, check modules, case IDs, fixtures, unit boundaries, requirements, selected entry points, configuration, result history, and explicit adequacy gaps connected to source definitions and public contracts.
major_error_concepts: Searching matching test filenames and assuming every public behavior is observed.
cards.prompt: Define Codebase executable-check map. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
required_concepts: A codebase executable-check map records discovery roots, check modules, and case identifiers.
The map records fixtures, unit boundaries, and execution requirements.
The map records selected entry points, configuration, and result history.
The map connects checks to source definitions and supported public contracts.
The map records explicit gaps in check adequacy.

cards.definition: **Definition.** The specified locations, schemas, readers, defaults, environment keys, parser overrides, precedence rules, tool namespaces, consumers, validation points, and sensitive-value nonclaims for every admitted configuration surface.
major_error_concepts: Searching key spelling alone and missing aliases, computed lookups, or defaults.
cards.prompt: Define Codebase configuration map. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
required_concepts: A codebase configuration map records every admitted configuration location and schema.
The map records readers, defaults, environment keys, and parser overrides.
The map records precedence rules, tool namespaces, and consuming components.
The map records validation points for effective configuration values.
The map states nonclaims about sensitive values not admitted to the evidence set.

cards.definition: **Definition.** The inventory of supported and internal path execution, module execution, package `__main__`, console scripts, plugin entry points, imported callable entries, and their source and distribution identities.
major_error_concepts: Searching only for main guards and missing metadata-defined entry points.
cards.prompt: Define Codebase entry-point map. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
required_concepts: A codebase entry-point map inventories supported and internal path executions.
The map inventories module execution and package `__main__` execution.
The map inventories console scripts, plugin entry points, and imported callable entries.
Each entry records its source identity and distribution identity.

cards.definition: **Definition.** The bounded union of static import sites, resolved qualified targets, conditional and dynamic candidates, runtime observed edges, cache behavior, failed imports, and explicitly unobserved surfaces for one release.
major_error_concepts: Calling parsed import statements the complete runtime dependency graph.
cards.prompt: Define Codebase import graph. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
required_concepts: A codebase import graph includes bounded static import sites and their resolved qualified targets.
The graph records conditional and dynamic import candidates.
The graph records runtime-observed import edges and cache behavior.
The graph records failed imports and explicitly unobserved surfaces.
Every graph claim is bound to one selected codebase release.

cards.definition: **Definition.** A versioned path, interface, configuration, generated artifact, runtime surface, or compatibility decision whose responsible maintainer or authority cannot be established from admitted evidence and must remain explicitly unresolved.
major_error_concepts: Inventing ownership from file location or recent commit proximity.
cards.prompt: Define Codebase ownership unknown. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
required_concepts: Codebase ownership unknown marks an admitted surface whose responsible maintainer or authority is not established by the evidence.
The unresolved surface may be a path, interface, configuration, generated artifact, runtime behavior, or compatibility decision.
The ownership question remains explicitly unresolved until admitted evidence identifies an authority.

cards.definition: **Definition.** The specified supported import paths, reexports, callable and class contracts, deprecations, documentation anchors, entry interfaces, and explicit internal exclusions reconciled across source and installed artifacts.
major_error_concepts: Listing every discovered definition as a supported public API.
cards.prompt: Define Codebase public API map. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
required_concepts: A codebase public API map records supported import paths and reexports.
The map records callable, class, and entry-interface contracts.
The map records deprecations and their documentation anchors.
The map records explicit internal exclusions from the supported API.
The map reconciles public surfaces across source and installed artifacts.

cards.definition: **Definition.** The admitted entry executions, imports, calls, configurations, resources, logs, files, exceptions, process outcomes, and installed-artifact observations covered by specified fixtures, with unexecuted paths and environments listed.
major_error_concepts: Equating possible source reachability with directly measured runtime behavior evidence.
cards.prompt: Define Codebase runtime surface map. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
required_concepts: A codebase runtime-surface map records admitted entry executions, imports, and calls.
The map records configurations, resources, logs, files, and exceptions observed by specified fixtures.
The map records process outcomes and installed-artifact observations.
The map explicitly lists unexecuted paths and untested environments.

cards.definition: **Definition.** The full set of case IDs, subtest accounting policy, loader failures, excluded candidates, and discovery configuration produced before optional selection or execution for one recorded run.
major_error_concepts: Reporting a pass percentage using only successful cases as the denominator.
cards.prompt: Define Collected check-case denominator. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
required_concepts: A collected check-case denominator contains the full set of collected case IDs.
The denominator states how subtests are accounted for.
The denominator records loader failures.
The denominator records excluded candidates.
The denominator records discovery configuration.
The denominator is frozen before optional case selection or execution.
The collected-case denominator belongs to one recorded check run.

cards.definition: **Definition.** A parser-level membership restriction applied to converted or raw values against a declared set, with display, equality, type conversion order, and domain completeness limitations explicit.
major_error_concepts: Calling a finite parser choice list complete validation of all application state.
cards.prompt: Define Command argument choice constraint. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
required_concepts: A command-choice constraint restricts a parsed argument to membership in a declared set.
The contract specifies how allowed choices are displayed to the user.
The contract specifies the equality or membership relation used for acceptance.
The contract specifies whether conversion occurs before membership testing.
The declared choice set limits accepted spellings but does not by itself establish completeness of the semantic domain.

cards.definition: **Definition.** An explicitly present parsed argument selected to replace or augment lower-precedence configuration values, with absence distinguished from a parser default that can accidentally erase provenance.
major_error_concepts: Applying every parser destination as an explicit override even when the user supplied nothing.
cards.prompt: Define Command-line configuration override. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
required_concepts: A command configuration override uses an explicitly present parsed argument to replace or augment a lower-precedence source.
The override rule specifies whether replacement or augmentation applies to the field.
Argument absence is distinct from a parser default that silently erases lower-source provenance.

cards.definition: **Definition.** The specified command and subcommand names, argument grammar, meanings, defaults, validation, configuration relations, outputs, diagnostics, return codes, side effects, and compatibility promises supported for external invocation.
major_error_concepts: Treating an example invocation as the complete supported command grammar.
cards.prompt: Define Command-line interface contract. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
required_concepts: A command contract declares the command and subcommand names accepted by an application.
The contract declares the accepted argument grammar.
The contract assigns meanings to accepted arguments.
The contract declares defaults for omitted arguments.
The contract declares validation rules for parsed values.
The contract declares how command arguments relate to other configuration sources.
The contract declares the application's output formats and diagnostic behavior.
The contract assigns meanings to return codes and observable side effects.
The contract states compatibility commitments for command consumers.

cards.definition: **Definition.** The parser-supplied value or absence behavior used when a declaration receives no matching vector input, kept distinct from application configuration defaults and conversion of explicit values.
major_error_concepts: Calling a parser default the provenance of every effective application value.
cards.prompt: Define Command argument default. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
required_concepts: A command default is the parser value or absence produced when the associated argument is not supplied.
The command default is distinct from an application-level default applied after parsing.
The declaration states whether explicit input is converted differently from the stored default.

cards.definition: **Definition.** The parser-result attribute or mapping key receiving a converted value from one or more declarations, with naming, collisions, defaults, and suppressed-storage behavior recorded.
major_error_concepts: Inferring result field names only from displayed option strings.
cards.prompt: Define Parsed argument destination. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
required_concepts: A command destination is the result attribute or mapping key that receives a converted value from one or more argument declarations.
The destination declaration records how the result attribute or mapping-key name is chosen.
The parser contract states how destination-name collisions are resolved.
The parser contract states how defaults populate the destination.
The parser contract states when destination storage is suppressed.

cards.definition: **Definition.** Application or parser logic checking semantic relationships beyond token grammar and basic conversion, with invalid-value disposition, diagnostic channel, return code, and side-effect ordering explicit.
major_error_concepts: Assuming successful parsing establishes every cross-field and environmental precondition.
cards.prompt: Define Command domain validation. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
required_concepts: Command-domain validation checks semantic constraints beyond argument grammar and type conversion.
The validation contract identifies each rejected value or cross-argument relation.
The validation contract identifies the diagnostic channel and process outcome for rejection.
The validation contract specifies whether any application side effect may occur before rejection.

cards.definition: **Definition.** An option-triggered parser action that sets, clears, counts, appends, or otherwise updates a destination without necessarily consuming a separate value token, with repeated-use semantics explicit.
major_error_concepts: Treating every option as consuming exactly one following argument.
cards.prompt: Define Command flag action. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
required_concepts: A command-flag action defines the state change caused by the presence of a declared option.
A flag action may set a value, clear a value, count occurrences, append a value, or perform another declared action.
Some flag actions consume no following value from the argument vector.
The action declaration specifies how repeated flag appearances affect the destination.

cards.definition: **Definition.** The specified usage, positional and optional argument descriptions, defaults where exposed, subcommand list, examples, exit behavior, and limitation text presented by parser-generated or custom help.
major_error_concepts: Treating successful help rendering as proof every documented invocation works.
cards.prompt: Define Command help contract. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
required_concepts: A command-help contract specifies the usage text shown for the command.
The help contract describes positional and optional arguments.
The help contract states which defaults are exposed to users.
The help contract describes available subcommands and representative examples.
The help contract specifies the stream and exit behavior for help requests.
The help contract states known limitations of the displayed documentation.
Command help may be generated by the parser or supplied by custom help logic.

cards.definition: **Definition.** A configured parser rejection caused by unrecognized, missing, malformed, conflicting, or choice-invalid argument input, with diagnostic text, usage emission, exception behavior, streams, and exit status recorded.
major_error_concepts: Reporting every nonzero command exit as a parse failure.
cards.prompt: Define Command parse failure. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
required_concepts: A command parse failure rejects an argument vector under the parser contract.
Rejection may result from an unrecognized, missing, malformed, conflicting, or disallowed argument.
The failure contract specifies the diagnostic and usage text produced on rejection.
The failure contract specifies any exception raised and the streams used for reporting.
The failure contract specifies the resulting process exit behavior.

cards.definition:
**Definition.** The recorded process stderr stream for parse messages, application errors, warnings, or logs as configured, with format stability and separation from statistical standard error, exception objects, and process status explicitly bounded.

**Worked check.** A CLI writes diagnostics to stderr and data to stdout; capture both streams separately so a successful data pipeline cannot parse an error line as output.
major_error_concepts: Treating stderr output as automatically indicating a nonzero exit or failed command.
cards.prompt: What does Command stderr-stream contract diagnose or distinguish?
required_concepts: Command standard error is the recorded diagnostic stream used for selected parse errors, application errors, warnings, or logs.
The command contract specifies which diagnostics are written to standard error and their format stability.
Command standard error is distinct from a statistical standard error.
Command standard error is distinct from an exception object and from the process exit status.

cards.definition: **Definition.** The specified user- or pipeline-facing text or bytes written to standard output, including format, ordering, terminators, stability, partial-output behavior, and separation from diagnostic logging.
major_error_concepts: Mixing debug logs into a promised machine-readable output stream.
cards.prompt: Define Command standard-output contract. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
required_concepts: Command standard output carries user-facing or pipeline-facing text or bytes produced by the application.
The command contract specifies standard-output format, ordering, and record terminators.
The command contract specifies which standard-output details are stable for consumers.
The command contract specifies whether partial standard output can precede a failure.
Standard output remains distinct from diagnostic logging unless the contract intentionally combines them.

cards.definition: **Definition.** The parser invocation of a declared conversion callable on selected argument strings, producing a value or parse-classified failure while retaining callable identity, input text, effects, and exception behavior.
major_error_concepts: Treating a type annotation on application code as argparse conversion.
cards.prompt: Define Command argument type conversion. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
required_concepts: Command type conversion applies a declared conversion callable to an argument string.
A successful conversion supplies the value stored for that argument.
A declared conversion failure becomes a parse failure under the parser contract.
The conversion record preserves callable identity, input text, side effects, and exception behavior.

cards.definition: **Definition.** The concise parser-rendered or custom syntax summary for one command branch, interpreted as documentation rather than a complete formal grammar or execution receipt.
major_error_concepts: Inferring every cardinality and semantic constraint from the usage line alone.
cards.prompt: Define Command usage line. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
required_concepts: A command usage line is a concise parser-rendered or custom notation for one command-syntax branch.
The usage line is documentation rather than a complete formal grammar.
The usage line is not evidence that the depicted invocation executed successfully.

accepted_variants: Keep from new import f in old, verify both old.f and new.f through the supported imports and behavior checks, and remove old.f only when the announced window and removal conditions are satisfied.
cards.definition: Retain an old-path binding, such as from new import f inside old. Check that both old.f and new.f import and satisfy the supported callable contract, using controlled fresh imports when initialization matters. Remove the bridge only under the announced deprecation/removal policy after the promised window and required migration conditions.
major_error_concepts: A reexport means move f to new, delete old immediately, and check only that new imports.
cards.prompt: Function f moves from module old to module new, but old is supported for one deprecation window. What binding, two import-path checks, and removal condition provide a compatibility reexport?
required_concepts: Retain the old import binding to the relocated supported object.
Check both old and new import routes and their promised behavior.
Gate removal on the stated deprecation window and migration/removal policy.

cards.definition: **Definition.** The affected consumer, relied-upon contract field, old and new behavior, evidence strength, severity, likelihood boundary, migration or compatibility candidate, and unresolved external-consumer uncertainty for one proposed change.
major_error_concepts: Assigning one risk level to an entire file change with no consumer relation.
cards.prompt: Define Change compatibility-risk record. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
required_concepts: A compatibility-risk record identifies the affected consumer and relied-upon contract field.
The record compares old and proposed behavior.
The record states evidence strength, severity, and the boundary of likelihood estimation.
The record identifies a migration or compatibility candidate when one is supported.
The record retains uncertainty about unobserved external consumers.

cards.definition: **Definition.** A specified object or component retaining and delegating to another object through an explicit field or constructor dependency rather than inheriting its implementation identity.
major_error_concepts: Calling any local object creation composition without recording ownership and delegation boundaries.
cards.prompt: Define Object composition relation. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
required_concepts: Object composition retains another object through an explicit field or constructor dependency.
The composing object delegates selected behavior to the retained object.
Composition does not inherit the retained object's implementation identity.

cards.definition: **Definition.** An import request reached only when a specified branch, platform, version, type-checking, or other runtime condition selects its containing path.
major_error_concepts: Reporting conditional availability as unconditional support across the entire project.
cards.prompt: Define Conditional import. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
required_concepts: An import request reached only when a specified branch, platform, version, type-checking, or other runtime condition selects its containing path.

cards.definition: **Definition.** The specified keys, nested structure, expected runtime value kinds, optionality, defaults, allowed unknown-key policy, relationships, and error dispositions required after source parsing.
major_error_concepts: Using TOML parse success alone as complete application schema validation.
cards.prompt: Define Application configuration schema. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
required_concepts: A configuration schema declares accepted keys and their nested structure.
The schema declares the value kinds and optionality of configuration fields.
The schema declares field defaults and the policy for unknown keys.
The schema declares required relationships among multiple fields.
The schema declares the errors produced for invalid configuration shapes or values.

cards.definition: **Definition.** The schema and cross-field checks applied to resolved values before application work, with rejected fields, source provenance, diagnostics, return status, and absence of unauthorized side effects recorded.
major_error_concepts: Validating each source independently while an invalid combination emerges only after precedence.
cards.prompt: Define Effective configuration validation. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
required_concepts: Configuration-domain validation applies field and cross-field constraints after configuration assembly.
Validation occurs before application work that depends on the configuration.
A rejection identifies the invalid field relationship and its source provenance.
A rejection specifies the diagnostic and application return status.
A rejected configuration causes no unauthorized application side effects.

cards.definition: **Definition.** The specified field-specific order and merge or replacement semantics among built-in, file, environment, command, and other authorized sources, including invalid-source behavior and provenance retention.
major_error_concepts: Saying CLI wins without defining absent values, nested merging, or invalid overrides.
cards.prompt: Define Configuration precedence rule. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
required_concepts: A configuration precedence rule orders built-in, file, environment, command, and other declared sources for each field.
The rule specifies merge or replacement behavior when multiple sources supply a field.
The rule specifies the disposition of invalid values from a candidate source.
The rule preserves provenance for the winning and shadowed candidate values.

cards.definition: **Definition.** Effective application configuration is the validated result of combining defaults, configuration files, environment values, and command-line overrides according to declared precedence and provenance rules.
major_error_concepts: Recording only final values while losing which source supplied or overrode each value.
cards.prompt: Define effective application configuration. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
required_concepts: A configuration release is the validated configuration selected for one application execution.
The release may combine built-in defaults, configuration files, process-environment values, and command arguments.
The release records the precedence and merge rules used to combine sources.
The release records the provenance of every effective configuration value.

cards.definition: **Definition.** The target-environment command path, generated wrapper provenance, argument vector, loaded entry object, configuration, stdout, stderr, logs, return, process exit, and side effects for one installed console-script execution.
major_error_concepts: Calling metadata discovery proof that the generated console command works.
cards.prompt: Define Installed console-command readback. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
required_concepts: Installed console-command readback identifies the target-environment command path and generated-wrapper provenance.
The readback records the argument vector and loaded entry object.
The readback records the resolved application configuration.
The readback records standard output, standard error, and log observations.
The readback records the application return, process exit status, and observable side effects.

accepted_variants: [project.scripts] can map hello to pkg.cli:main; it becomes a console_scripts entry. The installer supplies command integration, but metadata alone does not demonstrate a successful import or run.
cards.definition: A [project.scripts] entry maps a command name to an object reference, producing an entry in the console_scripts group. Installers use that metadata to provide platform-appropriate command integration. The declaration alone does not prove the referenced callable imports or runs successfully.
major_error_concepts: The standardized entry-point group is console-scripts, and merely listing the command proves its callable executes.
cards.prompt: What metadata maps a Python installed console command to an entry callable, and what does that declaration not prove?
required_concepts: Map command name to object reference through project.scripts/console_scripts metadata.
Installed command execution and callable validity still require separate checks.

cards.definition: **Definition.** A type parameter whose solutions are limited to one of a declared finite set of types under checker inference, differing from an upper bound and from an arbitrary union parameter.
major_error_concepts: Assuming constraints preserve every concrete subtype exactly like an upper bound.
cards.prompt: Define Constrained type parameter. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
required_concepts: A constrained type parameter has solutions limited to a declared finite set of types.
The configured checker selects among those solutions during inference.
A finite constraint set is distinct from a single upper bound.
A constrained type parameter is distinct from an arbitrary union-typed parameter.

cards.definition: **Definition.** A required collaborator provided during instance construction under a declared callable or protocol contract, ownership rule, lifetime, and failure policy.
major_error_concepts: Passing a collaborator without defining which methods or behavior the consumer requires.
cards.prompt: Define Constructor-supplied dependency. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
required_concepts: A required collaborator provided during instance construction under a declared callable or protocol contract, ownership rule, lifetime, and failure policy.

cards.definition: **Definition.** A generic interface using a type parameter in input-compatible positions so a consumer able to accept a supertype can be assignable where a consumer of the subtype is expected.
major_error_concepts: Reversing the assignability direction because the word subtype appears in the requested interface.
cards.prompt: Define Contravariant consumer interface. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
required_concepts: A contravariant consumer uses its type parameter in input-compatible positions.
A consumer that accepts a supertype can then be assignable where a consumer of the subtype is expected.
Contravariant-consumer assignability remains subject to the declared generic and checker rules.

cards.definition: **Definition.** The checker-inferred types and reachability facts associated with bindings at one source program point after accounting for preceding branches, assignments, exits, assertions, and exceptional control under a recorded analysis.
major_error_concepts: Assigning one global inferred type to a variable across every control-flow location.
cards.prompt: Define Control-flow static type state. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
required_concepts: Control-flow static type state records inferred binding types at one source program point.
The state records reachability facts at that point.
The state accounts for preceding branches.
The state accounts for preceding assignments.
The state accounts for preceding exits and assertions.
The state accounts for exceptional control flow.
The state is bound to one recorded checker analysis.

cards.definition: **Definition.** A versioned edit limited to the declared contract or implementation mechanism while unrelated formatting, dependencies, tools, fixtures, configuration, and environment remain fixed enough for before-after attribution.
major_error_concepts: Combining structural refactor, dependency updates, and behavior changes into one impact experiment.
cards.prompt: Define Controlled code change. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
required_concepts: A controlled code change is a versioned edit limited to the declared contract or implementation mechanism.
Unrelated formatting, dependencies, tools, fixtures, and configuration remain fixed enough for comparison.
The execution environment remains fixed enough to attribute observed differences to the declared edit.

cards.definition: **Definition.** A generic interface using a type parameter in output-compatible positions so an instance producing a subtype can be assignable where a producer of the supertype is expected under specified rules.
major_error_concepts: Declaring covariance on an interface that also accepts arbitrary values of the same parameter type.
cards.prompt: Define Covariant producer interface. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
required_concepts: A covariant producer uses its type parameter in output-compatible positions.
A producer of a subtype can then be assignable where a producer of the supertype is expected.
Covariant-producer assignability remains subject to the declared generic and checker rules.

cards.definition: **Definition.** The specific active initialization path, recursive request, cache hit, requested binding, and missing-or-stale state that connects an import-cycle component to a specified failure.
major_error_concepts: Repairing arbitrary import syntax without identifying the order-sensitive unavailable state.
cards.prompt: Define Circular-import failure mechanism. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
required_concepts: A circular-import failure mechanism identifies the active module-initialization path.
The mechanism identifies the recursive import request on that path.
The mechanism identifies the relevant module-cache hit.
The mechanism identifies the binding requested from the partially initialized module.
The mechanism identifies the missing or stale state observed at that point.
The traced initialization facts connect an import-cycle component to one specified runtime failure.

cards.definition: **Definition.** A bounded change to dependency direction, shared interface placement, import timing, or public surface predicted to remove the specified partial-initialization mechanism with compatibility effects stated.
major_error_concepts: Moving an import inside a function and calling the design repaired without evaluating repeated runtime behavior and dependencies.
cards.prompt: Define Circular-import repair candidate. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
required_concepts: A circular-import repair candidate is a bounded change to dependency direction, shared-interface placement, import timing, or the public surface.
The candidate predicts how that change removes the specified partial-initialization mechanism.
The candidate states the resulting compatibility effects.

cards.definition: **Definition.** Import-system location of a qualified module or package followed by execution in the initial top-level environment while retaining package-aware metadata needed by relative imports.
major_error_concepts: Describing `-m` as merely opening a path with an alternative spelling.
cards.prompt: Define `python -m` module execution. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
required_concepts: `python -m` execution asks the import system to locate a qualified module or package.
The selected code is then executed in the initial top-level environment.
The execution retains package-aware metadata.
The retained package metadata supports explicit relative imports.

accepted_variants: P('bad') gives fields x='bad' and y=0, represented as P(x='bad', y=0). dataclass does not enforce the int annotation.
cards.definition: The default dataclass options generate initialization, representation and field equality where not overridden. P('bad') stores the string in x and 0 in y; its ordinary representation is P(x='bad', y=0). Dataclass field annotations are not runtime type validators. It remains a Python class with normal user methods and inheritance.
major_error_concepts: P('bad') raises a type error automatically because dataclass enforces x: int at runtime.
cards.prompt:
What does P('bad') produce here, and does x: int enforce the value's runtime type?
```python
from dataclasses import dataclass
@dataclass
class P:
    x: int
    y: int = 0
```
required_concepts: The generated initializer accepts 'bad' as x and supplies y=0; the representation exposes those field values.
The int annotation itself does not reject the string at runtime.

accepted_variants: Use items: list[int] = field(default_factory=list). For a=Bag() and b=Bag(), (a.items is b.items) evaluates to False; equality of their initially empty contents would not test aliasing.
cards.definition: Declare items: list[int] = field(default_factory=list) in a dataclass. The zero-argument list factory is invoked for each omitted value during generated initialization. For a=Bag() and b=Bag(), (a.items is b.items) evaluates to False. A general factory is not guaranteed to return distinct objects unless its behavior does so.
major_error_concepts: Use field(default_factory=list()) or one shared list object and verify only a.items == b.items.
cards.prompt: Two Bag instances omit a mutable items field. Which dataclass declaration gives each its own list, and what identity test verifies that?
required_concepts: Use field(default_factory=list) or an equivalent zero-argument factory that creates a fresh list per instance.
Check (a.items is b.items) is False, not merely value equality.

cards.definition: **Definition.** Dataclass-generated equality compares fields with compare=True in declaration order only when the other object has the identical runtime type; it is distinct from identity, hashing, ordering, and domain equivalence.
major_error_concepts: Calling generated field equality a complete semantic domain-equivalence proof.
cards.prompt: Define Dataclass generated equality. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
required_concepts: Dataclass-generated equality compares fields whose `compare` option is true.
Dataclass-generated equality compares the selected fields in declaration order.
Generated equality requires the other object to have the identical runtime type.
Generated equality is distinct from object identity.
Generated equality is distinct from hashing and generated ordering.
Generated equality does not by itself establish domain-specific equivalence.

accepted_variants: A field describes a data attribute plus generation options such as init, repr, compare and kw_only. init=False can remove its constructor parameter; a required field can have no default at all.
cards.definition: A dataclass field records a declared data attribute and options controlling generated behavior. Its metadata can govern initialization, representation, comparison, keyword-only status and a default or factory when present. init=False omits it from generated initializer parameters, and required fields can have no default.
major_error_concepts: Every dataclass field must become an __init__ parameter and must record a default or default_factory.
cards.prompt: What does a dataclass field describe, and do all fields appear as initializer parameters or have defaults?
required_concepts: A field describes a data attribute plus options governing generated dataclass behavior.
Not every field has an initializer parameter or default: init=False and required no-default fields are valid.

accepted_variants: It compares selected fields lexicographically for identical types, not arbitrary base/subclass pairs. order=True needs eq=True and cannot coexist with explicit ordering methods.
cards.definition: With order=True, dataclass generates lexicographic ordering over comparison-enabled fields in declaration order. Both operands must have identical runtime type for this generated comparison. order=True requires eq=True; defining an ordering method while also requesting generated ordering raises an error. Field order is not automatically a meaningful domain order.
major_error_concepts: Generated ordering treats every subclass instance as interchangeable with a base instance and works with order=True, eq=False.
cards.prompt: What does dataclass order=True generate, which objects can it compare, and what option conflicts matter?
required_concepts: Generated ordering is lexicographic over selected fields and requires identical operand types.
order=True with eq=False is invalid; conflicts with user-defined ordering methods are invalid.

cards.definition: **Definition.** The optional method called by a generated initializer after generated field assignments, available for derived state or validation while retaining partial-state and exception effects.
major_error_concepts: Assuming the hook runs when a user-defined initializer replaces the generated call path.
cards.prompt: Define Dataclass post-initialization hook. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
required_concepts: A dataclass post-initialization hook is an optional method called by a generated initializer.
The call occurs after generated field assignments.
The hook can compute derived state or validate the initialized state.
The hook contract accounts for partially initialized state.
The hook contract accounts for effects that remain when the hook raises an exception.

cards.definition: **Definition.** Creation of a new dataclass instance by supplying selected changed fields through the class's initialization path, with post-init behavior, non-init fields, and shallow referenced-object sharing considered.
major_error_concepts: Calling replacement a deep immutable update with no constructor effects.
cards.prompt: Define Dataclass replacement construction. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
required_concepts: Dataclass replacement constructs a new instance.
Selected changed fields are supplied through the class's initialization path.
Replacement accounts for post-initialization behavior.
Replacement accounts for fields excluded from generated initialization.
Unchanged referenced objects may remain shallowly shared between the old and new instances.

cards.definition:
**Definition.** The explicit separation among requirement declarations, marker evaluation, candidate discovery, resolver decisions, downloaded artifacts, installed distributions, import availability, and observed compatibility.

**Worked check.** A type checker can resolve an imported annotation from stubs while runtime import execution still fails; record which resolver and environment produced each result.
major_error_concepts: Calling valid dependency metadata a successfully resolved and installed environment.
cards.prompt: What boundary or limitation does Dependency declaration-resolution boundary impose?
required_concepts: The dependency declaration-resolution boundary separates requirement declarations from marker evaluation.
The boundary separates candidate discovery from resolver decisions and downloaded artifacts.
The boundary separates installed distributions from import availability.
The boundary separates all preceding packaging evidence from observed compatibility of executed behavior.

cards.definition: **Definition.** A Python default expression is evaluated once when the function definition executes and the resulting object is stored with the function; on a call that omits the argument, that stored object is bound to the parameter, so mutable defaults are shared across such calls.
major_error_concepts: Treating a default expression as if Python reevaluated it automatically on every call.
cards.prompt: Define default argument object. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
required_concepts: A Python default expression is evaluated once when the function definition executes.
The resulting default object is stored with the function.
When a call omits the argument, the stored object is bound to the parameter.
A mutable stored default is therefore shared across calls that omit that argument.

accepted_variants: The request occurs later. First initialization is delayed only if no earlier path loads the module; otherwise the request can be a cache hit. Failure timing, repeated lookup overhead, dependency visibility and annotation needs can change.
cards.definition: Deferral moves when that import request is reached. It can delay first initialization and failures if the module is not already loaded; if another path has initialized it, the deferred request may simply hit the cache. Repeated request cost, dependency visibility and static annotation needs must still be considered.
major_error_concepts: Moving an import into a function guarantees that no other path can initialize its module before that function runs.
cards.prompt: What can change when an import is moved inside a later call, and is module initialization necessarily postponed?
required_concepts: Separate the delayed request from first module initialization, which might already have happened elsewhere.
Describe possible failure-timing, repeated lookup and visibility/type-checking tradeoffs.

cards.definition: **Definition.** A specified source or generated occurrence resolved or conservatively linked to a qualified definition through syntax, name binding, import, attribute access, type information, or runtime identity, with confidence and ambiguity recorded.
major_error_concepts: Calling every textual spelling match a semantic reference to the same definition.
cards.prompt: Define Definition reference. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
required_concepts: A definition reference is a specified source or generated occurrence linked to a qualified definition or candidate definitions.
The link may use syntax, name binding, imports, attribute access, type information, or runtime identity.
The record distinguishes a resolved link from a conservative candidate link.
The record preserves confidence and ambiguity in the relation.

cards.definition: **Definition.** The attempt to recover source text and location for a recorded runtime object using documented inspection interfaces, with wrappers, generated code, interactive definitions, built-ins, missing source, and retrieval exceptions recorded.
major_error_concepts: Treating unavailable source as proof the object has no implementation.
cards.prompt: Define Definition source retrieval. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
required_concepts: Definition source retrieval is an attempt to recover source text and location for a recorded runtime object.
The attempt uses documented inspection interfaces under a specified environment.
The result records wrapper and generated-code relationships.
The result records interactive definitions, built-ins, missing source, and retrieval exceptions when encountered.

cards.definition: **Definition.** A standardized group entry incorporating another named dependency group into the expanded requirement list, with normalization, cycles, duplicate retention, order, and tool handling considered.
major_error_concepts: Treating inclusion as copying a resolved or locked dependency graph.
cards.prompt: Define Dependency-group inclusion. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
required_concepts: A dependency-group inclusion is a standardized entry that incorporates another named group into an expanded requirement list.
Group-name normalization applies while resolving the inclusion.
Expansion behavior records ordering and retention of duplicate requirements.
Expansion detects inclusion cycles and records the tool's failure or handling behavior.

cards.definition: **Definition.** A named list in the standardized dependency-groups table for development or task-specific requirements not included in built distribution metadata as project dependencies merely by declaration.
major_error_concepts: Calling a dependency group an installable package extra for end users.
cards.prompt: Define Development dependency group. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
required_concepts: A development dependency group is a named requirement list in the standardized dependency-groups table.
The group supports development or task-specific environments.
Merely declaring the group does not include its requirements as project dependencies in built distribution metadata.

cards.definition: **Definition.** A still-supported public member marked for future removal or behavior change with replacement, notice mechanism, affected release range, and current compatibility status recorded.
major_error_concepts: Calling a removed or silently broken name deprecated after compatibility has already ended.
cards.prompt: Define Deprecated public name. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
required_concepts: A deprecated public name remains supported in the current release.
The deprecation marks the member for a future removal or behavior change.
The deprecation identifies the supported replacement.
The deprecation records how consumers are notified.
The deprecation records the affected release range.
The deprecation records the member's current compatibility status.

cards.definition: **Definition.** The explicit release, audience, old behavior, replacement, warning channel, planned removal condition, and unpromised surfaces delimiting one deprecation claim.
major_error_concepts: Announcing vague future change with no affected identity or replacement path.
cards.prompt: Define API deprecation boundary. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
required_concepts: The explicit release, audience, old behavior, replacement, warning channel, planned removal condition, and unpromised surfaces delimiting one deprecation claim.

cards.definition: **Definition.** A qualified callable object or candidate set selected by one call site after binding, lookup, dispatch, and wrapper relations are considered, with runtime observation and static possibility kept distinct.
major_error_concepts: Naming the syntactic attribute as a unique callee without dispatch evidence.
cards.prompt: Define Direct callee. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
required_concepts: A direct callee is the qualified callable or candidate set selected by one call site.
Callee selection accounts for binding, lookup, dispatch, and wrapper relations.
The callee record distinguishes a runtime-observed target from a statically possible target.

cards.definition: **Definition.** A specified function, method, module body, entry wrapper, or generated unit containing a call site confirmed or conservatively linked to a target callable under specified static or runtime evidence.
major_error_concepts: Calling a module a direct caller when the actual call lives in an unreached nested function.
cards.prompt: Define Direct caller. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
required_concepts: A direct caller is a specified executable unit containing a call site linked to the target callable.
The executable unit may be a function, method, module body, entry wrapper, or generated unit.
The caller relation records whether its support is confirmed or conservative.
The caller relation records the static or runtime evidence used for the link.

cards.definition: **Definition.** A specified import, call, construction, subclass, protocol use, configuration reader, metadata consumer, check, documentation path, or entry wrapper directly dependent on a changed target field under admitted evidence.
major_error_concepts: Counting files instead of the exact dependency relation each consumer uses.
cards.prompt: Define Direct change consumer. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
required_concepts: A direct change consumer is an admitted surface that immediately depends on a changed contract field.
The surface may be an import, call, construction, subclass, protocol use, configuration reader, or metadata consumer.
The surface may instead be a check, documentation path, or entry wrapper.
The dependency relation remains bounded to the admitted navigation evidence.

cards.definition: **Definition.** One evidence-backed importer-to-target relation caused by a specific reached import request, annotated with source site, condition, execution phase, result, and whether the target was newly initialized or cached.
major_error_concepts: Treating every syntactic import as reached in every execution.
cards.prompt: Define Direct import edge. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
required_concepts: A direct import edge is an evidence-backed relation from one importer to one target.
The edge is caused by a specific import request that was reached.
The edge records the request's source site.
The edge records the condition under which the request was reached.
The edge records the execution phase.
The edge records the request result.
The edge records whether the target was newly initialized or supplied from cache.

cards.definition: **Definition.** A candidate source path successfully mapped and imported under a qualified name for check loading, with origin, cache prestate, import effects, and loading errors preserved.
major_error_concepts: Counting a matching filename before proving which module object was imported.
cards.prompt: Define Discovered check-module identity. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
required_concepts: A discovered check-module identity begins with a candidate source path.
The path is successfully mapped to a qualified module name.
The module is successfully imported for check loading.
The record preserves the selected module origin.
The record preserves module-cache prestate and import-time effects.
The record preserves loading errors associated with discovery.

cards.definition: **Definition.** The versioned filename matching rule used to select candidate check modules during discovery, distinct from test-method name rules and from successful import or collection.
major_error_concepts: Assuming all Python files beneath the discovery root are collected.
cards.prompt: Define unittest discovery filename pattern. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
required_concepts: A unittest discovery filename pattern is a versioned matching rule for candidate check modules.
The pattern selects candidate filenames during discovery.
The filename pattern is distinct from test-method naming rules.
Matching the pattern does not prove successful module import or case collection.

cards.definition: **Definition.** The versioned filesystem location from which recursive check discovery begins, interpreted with a top-level directory, importability rules, pattern, working directory, and package structure.
major_error_concepts: Reporting discovery results without preserving the start and top-level directories.
cards.prompt: Define unittest discovery start directory. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
required_concepts: A unittest discovery start directory is a versioned filesystem location where recursive discovery begins.
Discovery interprets that location with a declared top-level directory.
Discovery applies the relevant importability rules.
Discovery applies a declared filename pattern.
Discovery records the process working directory.
Discovery records the package structure used to derive module identities.

cards.definition: **Definition.** The versioned directory used to derive importable module names for discovered files and inserted or interpreted for import resolution, with source-tree identity and shadowing risks explicit.
major_error_concepts: Deriving module identity from the discovery start directory alone.
cards.prompt: Define unittest discovery top-level directory. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
required_concepts: A unittest discovery top-level directory is versioned.
The directory is used to derive importable module names for discovered files.
The directory is inserted or interpreted for import resolution according to runner semantics.
The directory is bound to an identified source tree.
The configuration records import-shadowing risks.

cards.definition: **Definition.** The metadata-defined installable project name and version used by packaging tools and installed-distribution records, kept distinct from repository name, project root, and import names.
major_error_concepts: Deriving the installed distribution name from an import statement.
cards.prompt: Define Distribution project identity. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
required_concepts: Distribution-project identity is the metadata-defined installable project name and version.
Packaging tools use that identity.
Installed-distribution records use that identity.
Distribution-project identity is distinct from the repository name and project-root path.
Distribution-project identity is distinct from the project's import names.

cards.definition: **Definition.** An option allowing a marker in expected output to match any substring, increasing tolerance while potentially hiding meaningful values, ordering, exceptions, or omitted evidence.
major_error_concepts: Replacing most expected output with ellipses and calling the example verified.
cards.prompt: Define Doctest ellipsis matching. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
required_concepts: Doctest ellipsis matching allows a marker in expected output to match any substring.
The option increases matching tolerance.
Doctest ellipsis tolerance can hide meaningful values, ordering, exceptions, or omitted evidence.

cards.definition: **Definition.** A discovered interactive-style source example with prompts, executable input, expected output, option flags, namespace, source location, and runner context interpreted by doctest matching rules.
major_error_concepts: Treating every code block in documentation as an automatically collected doctest.
cards.prompt: Define Doctest example. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
required_concepts: A doctest example is a discovered interactive-style source example.
The example records prompt text.
The example records executable input.
The example records expected output.
The example records option flags.
The example records the execution namespace.
The example records its source location.
The example records runner context.
The runner interprets the example under doctest matching rules.

cards.definition: **Definition.** An interactive-style example whose expected output describes an exception traceback under doctest matching rules, with exception class and selected detail preserved but traceback formatting limits explicit.
major_error_concepts: Accepting any exception merely because expected output contains the word traceback.
cards.prompt: Define Doctest exception example. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
required_concepts: A doctest exception example is an interactive-style example whose expected output describes an exception traceback.
The runner compares the traceback under doctest matching rules.
The expectation preserves the exception class and selected details.
The expectation states limits on traceback-format matching.

cards.definition: **Definition.** The specified text representation expected after an example executes, compared through doctest's selected normalization and option behavior rather than object equality or semantic result comparison.
major_error_concepts: Calling matching displayed text proof that hidden object state is correct.
cards.prompt: Define Doctest expected output. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
required_concepts: Doctest expected output is a specified text representation expected after an example executes.
The runner compares the text using selected doctest normalization and option behavior.
The comparison is not ordinary Python object equality.
The comparison does not automatically establish semantic equality of results.

cards.definition: **Definition.** Multiple output emissions derived from one record because overlapping handlers, repeated configuration, propagation, or accidental multiple logging calls route it more than intended under the configured topology.
major_error_concepts: Deduplicating text after emission without repairing the routing mechanism.
cards.prompt: Define Duplicate log emission. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
required_concepts: A duplicate log record is multiple unintended emissions attributable to one logical logging event.
Duplication may arise from overlapping handlers, repeated configuration, enabled propagation, or repeated logging calls.
The configured logger-handler topology and logging-call count distinguish possible duplication mechanisms.

cards.definition:
**Definition.** The unresolved callee possibilities introduced by runtime types, protocols, inheritance, descriptors, registries, callbacks, entry points, plugins, computed names, or monkey patching beyond admitted static and runtime evidence.

**Worked check.** A call through `getattr(obj,name)` with input-derived `name` may be invisible to a closed static call graph; bound the reported graph to resolved targets.
major_error_concepts: Collapsing an open extension surface to the single implementation observed once.
cards.prompt: What boundary or limitation does Dynamic-dispatch analysis limit impose?
required_concepts: A dynamic-dispatch analysis limit records unresolved callee possibilities beyond the admitted evidence.
Uncertainty may arise from runtime types, protocols, inheritance, descriptors, registries, or callbacks.
Entry points, plugins, computed names, and monkey patching may add further candidates.
The limit separates statically possible and runtime-observed dispatch from unexamined alternatives.

cards.definition: **Definition.** A module request whose target name or timing is computed at runtime through an import interface rather than fixed entirely by ordinary import-statement syntax.
major_error_concepts: Omitting computed imports from impact analysis because no matching import statement exists.
cards.prompt: Define Dynamic import request. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
required_concepts: A module request whose target name or timing is computed at runtime through an import interface rather than fixed entirely by ordinary import-statement syntax.

accepted_variants: A supported backend can extend a dependencies list that has static entries and is also listed in dynamic, preserving those entries. The final list still needs backend readback; this PEP808 exception does not allow both static and dynamic scalar version values.
cards.definition: A field listed in project.dynamic delegates determination of its final metadata to the backend. Under PEP808/current PyPA rules, eligible list/table fields may include static entries as an append-only starting portion; the backend may add but not remove, reorder or modify those entries. Scalar fields do not gain this exception. The chosen backend must support the adopted rules, and final values require artifact readback.
major_error_concepts: Every dynamic field must have no static entries under current rules, or the backend may freely replace static entries once dynamic is listed.
cards.prompt: What does dynamic project metadata delegate to the build backend, and can an eligible dynamic field include static entries under PEP808?
required_concepts: Dynamic marks backend participation in final metadata; it need not mean every entry is absent from pyproject.
Eligible list/table static portions can coexist under PEP808 with append-only preservation, subject to backend support; do not extend this to scalars.

cards.definition: **Definition.** The value selected for one schema field after source parsing, conversion, precedence, merge, and validation, paired with winning provenance and shadowed candidates rather than detached from its resolution history.
major_error_concepts: Logging only the final value and making configuration disputes impossible to audit.
cards.prompt: Define Effective configuration value. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
required_concepts: An effective configuration value is the selected value for one field after parsing, conversion, precedence, merge, and validation.
The value records the source provenance that won selection.
The effective configuration value is paired with lower-precedence candidates that were shadowed.

cards.definition: **Definition.** The threshold obtained from a logger's explicit level or nearest configured ancestor according to hierarchy rules, evaluated before handler thresholds and other filtering.
major_error_concepts: Reading only the child's level field and predicting record emission.
cards.prompt: Define Effective logger level. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
required_concepts: A logger's effective level is its explicit level or the nearest explicit ancestor level found through inheritance.
The effective level participates in deciding whether a logging call creates a record.
The effective logger-level decision occurs before handler-level and filter decisions.

cards.definition: **Definition.** A callable entry boundary that accepts specified arguments or dependencies, performs application work only when invoked, returns an application status, and can be imported without automatically running that work.
major_error_concepts: Hiding global argument reads and process exit inside import-time code while naming another wrapper `main`.
cards.prompt: Define Import-safe main function. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
required_concepts: An import-safe main function is a callable application-entry boundary.
The function accepts specified arguments or injected dependencies.
The function performs application work only when invoked.
The function returns an application status.
Importing the function's module does not automatically invoke that application work.

cards.definition: **Definition.** A consumer-defined namespace collecting installed entry points for one discovery purpose, with group naming, collision policy, accepted object interface, and security limitations defined by that consumer.
major_error_concepts: Assuming every entry-point group creates an executable shell command.
cards.prompt: Define Distribution entry-point group. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
required_concepts: A distribution entry-point group is a consumer-defined namespace for one discovery purpose.
The consumer defines valid group naming and the accepted interface of loaded objects.
The consumer defines collision handling among records in the group.
The consumer defines security limitations for discovering and loading group entries.

cards.definition: **Definition.** The installed metadata triple of group, name, and object reference plus distribution provenance, optional extras, and parsed module and attribute components used for discovery and loading.
major_error_concepts: Loading an entry-point object before recording its owning distribution and collision context.
cards.prompt: Define Distribution entry-point record. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
required_concepts: A distribution entry-point record stores an installed group, name, and object reference.
The record retains provenance to its owning distribution.
The record may include optional extras associated with loading.
The record exposes parsed module and attribute components for discovery and loading.

cards.definition: **Definition.** The declared set of distribution names, versions, metadata locations, files where available, requirements, entry points, and import-name mappings visible to one environment interpreter.
major_error_concepts: Treating declared project dependencies as evidence of what is actually installed.
cards.prompt: Define Environment installed-distribution inventory. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
required_concepts: An environment installed-distribution inventory is observed through one selected environment interpreter.
The inventory records distribution names, versions, and metadata locations.
The inventory records installed files when that metadata is available.
The inventory records declared requirements and installed entry points.
The inventory records mappings from distribution names to import names when available.

cards.definition: **Definition.** The explicit executable path or resolved command that selects a virtual environment's Python for one invocation, kept distinct from shell activation and directory naming.
major_error_concepts: Assuming the command `python` resolves to the intended environment because its prompt looks activated.
cards.prompt: Define Environment interpreter selection. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
required_concepts: Environment interpreter selection records the explicit executable path or resolved command used for one Python invocation.
The selected executable determines which virtual environment's interpreter is invoked.
Interpreter selection is distinct from modifying a shell through activation.
Interpreter selection is distinct from the name of the directory containing the environment.

cards.definition: **Definition.** A standardized Boolean condition over declared environment properties controlling whether a requirement applies in a target context, with variables, comparison semantics, extras context, and evaluated result recorded.
major_error_concepts: Treating a marker as a runtime conditional import inside application code.
cards.prompt: Define Dependency environment marker. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
required_concepts: A dependency environment marker is a standardized Boolean condition over declared environment properties.
The marker determines whether its requirement applies in a selected target context.
The marker record includes referenced variables and comparison semantics.
The marker record includes any extras context and the evaluated Boolean result.

cards.definition: **Definition.** The explicit parsing of a selected environment string into the schema-required value kind with accepted spellings, empty handling, errors, provenance, and no inference from annotation alone.
major_error_concepts: Calling `bool(environment_text)` a reliable parser for Boolean configuration values.
cards.prompt: Define Environment configuration conversion. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
required_concepts: Environment-value conversion explicitly parses an environment string into a configuration-schema value kind.
The conversion contract declares accepted spellings and the treatment of empty strings.
The conversion contract declares errors for malformed values.
The converted value retains provenance to its environment key.
Type annotations alone do not infer environment-value conversion behavior.

cards.definition: **Definition.** An assertion applying equality semantics and runner-provided diagnostics to specified expected and observed objects, distinct from identity, approximate numeric relation, membership, ordering, and representation equality.
major_error_concepts: Using equality where aliasing or object identity is the actual requirement.
cards.prompt: Define Equality assertion. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
required_concepts: An equality assertion applies equality semantics to specified expected and observed objects.
The runner supplies diagnostics for an equality mismatch.
Equality is distinct from identity, approximate numeric relation, membership, ordering, and representation equality.

cards.definition: **Definition.** A selected case whose setup, body, or cleanup raises an exception outside the runner's assertion-failure classification, with phase, traceback, partial observations, and remaining lifecycle behavior recorded.
major_error_concepts: Combining errors with failed expectations and losing whether the unit was exercised.
